units.zh: ◎藩鎮淄青橫海李正己，高麗人。
units.en: In the biographies of the Ziqing and Henghai buffer regions, Li Zhengji was of Koguryo descent.
units.literal: Buffer Regions: Ziqing and Henghai. Li Zhengji was a man of Goguryeo origin.

units.zh: 為營州副將，從侯希逸入青州，希逸母即其姑，故薦為折沖都尉。
units.en: He had been deputy commander at Yingzhou and followed Hou Xiyi into Qingzhou; because Xiyi's mother was his aunt, Xiyi recommended him as regimental commander of the Zhechong unit.
units.literal: He served as deputy general of Ying Prefecture, followed Hou Xiyi into Qing Prefecture; Xiyi's mother was his paternal aunt, so he was recommended as commander of the Zhechong regiment.

units.zh: 寶應中，以軍候從討史朝義。
units.en: During the Baoying reign (762–763), he served as a military scout in the campaign against Shi Chaoyi.
units.literal: In the Baoying era, as a military scout he followed the campaign against Shi Chaoyi.

units.zh: 時回紇恃功橫，諸軍莫敢抗。
units.en: The Uyghurs, flush with their victories, threw their weight around, and no allied army dared stand up to them.
units.literal: At that time the Uyghurs relied on their merit and acted overbearingly; none of the armies dared resist.

units.zh: 正己欲以氣折之，與大酋角逐，眾土皆墻立觀，約曰：「後者批之。」
units.en: Zhengji meant to humble them by sheer nerve and challenged the Uyghur chieftain to a footrace; the troops lined the walls to watch, with the wager that "whoever finished second would have his face struck."
units.literal: Zhengji wished to break their spirit by force of will; he raced the great chieftain, and all the men stood along the wall watching, with the agreement: "Whoever comes in behind gets his face slapped."

units.zh: 既逐而先，正己批其頰，回紇矢液流離，眾軍哄然笑。
units.en: Though he had chased from behind, he crossed the line first and slapped the chieftain across the face; the Uyghur was left trembling and drenched in sweat, and the whole army roared with laughter.
units.literal: Having overtaken him yet arriving first, Zhengji slapped his cheek; the Uyghur was drenched in sweat and urine, and the armies burst into laughter.

units.zh: 酋大慚，自是沮憚不敢暴。
units.en: The chieftain was utterly humiliated; thereafter the Uyghurs were cowed and no longer dared abuse their position.
units.literal: The chieftain was deeply shamed; from then on he was discouraged and afraid and did not dare act violently.

units.zh: 希逸以為兵馬使，沈毅得眾心，然陰忌之，因事解其職。
units.en: Xiyi made him director of military affairs; his steady, resolute manner won the soldiers' loyalty, but Xiyi secretly resented him and found a pretext to strip him of his post.
units.literal: Xiyi appointed him military commissioner; his gravity and resolution won the hearts of the troops, yet Xiyi secretly envied him and removed him from office on a pretext.

units.zh: 軍中皆言不當廢，尋逐希逸出之，有詔代為節度使。
units.en: The troops protested that he should never have been removed; before long they expelled Xiyi, and an imperial edict installed Zhengji as military governor in his place.
units.literal: The army all said he should not have been dismissed; soon they drove Xiyi out, and an edict named him to replace him as military governor.

units.zh: 本名懷玉，至是賜今名，遂有淄、青、齊、海、登、萊、沂、密、德、棣十州，與田承嗣、薛嵩、李寶臣、梁崇義輔牙相倚。
units.en: Born Huaiyu, he now received the name Zhengji by imperial grant. He came to control ten prefectures—Zi, Qing, Qi, Hai, Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, De, and Di—and stood shoulder to shoulder with the buffer lords Tian Chengsi, Xue Song, Li Baochen, and Liang Chongyi.
units.literal: His original name was Huaiyu; at this time he was granted his present name. He then held the ten prefectures of Zi, Qing, Qi, Hai, Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, De, and Di, and with Tian Chengsi, Xue Song, Li Baochen, and Liang Chongyi he leaned on one another like cheek teeth.

units.zh: 嵩死，李靈耀反，諸道攻之，共披其地。
units.en: After Xue Song's death, Li Lingyao rose in revolt; the allied circuits besieged him and carved up his domain among themselves.
units.literal: When Song died, Li Lingyao rebelled; the various circuits attacked him and together stripped his territory.

units.zh: 正己復取曹、濮、徐、兗、鄆，凡十有五州。
units.en: Zhengji seized Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan, and Yun as well, bringing his holdings to fifteen prefectures.
units.literal: Zhengji again took Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan, and Yun, fifteen prefectures in all.

units.zh: 市渤海名馬，歲不絕，賦繇均約，號最強大。
units.en: He bought famed Bohai horses without interruption, kept taxes and labor service fair and predictable, and was reckoned the most powerful of the buffer lords.
units.literal: He traded for famous horses of Bohai year after year without cease; levies and corvée were even and measured, and he was called the strongest of all.

units.zh: 政令嚴酷，在所不敢偶語，威震鄰境。
units.en: His rule was mercilessly strict—no one in his territory dared whisper in company—and his authority terrified the neighboring provinces.
units.literal: His government orders were harsh; within his domain no one dared speak casually in pairs, and his might awed the neighboring circuits.

units.zh: 歷檢校司空，加同中書門下平章事，以司徒兼太子太保，封饒陽郡王。
units.en: He rose through acting Minister of Works, was added as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, served as Grand Mentor while also Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Raoyang commandery.
units.literal: He rose through acting Minister of Works, was added as co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, served as Grand Mentor while also Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Raoyang commandery.

units.zh: 請附屬籍，許之。
units.en: He petitioned to be entered on the imperial clan rolls, and the court consented.
units.literal: He requested attachment to the imperial clan register; this was granted.

units.zh: 因徙治鄆，以子納及腹心將守諸州。
units.en: He shifted his headquarters to Yunzhou and left his son Li Na and his closest generals to hold the outlying prefectures.
units.literal: He therefore moved his seat of government to Yun, placing his son Na and trusted generals to guard the various prefectures.

units.zh: 建中初，聞城汴州，乃約田悅、梁崇義、李惟嶽偕叛。
units.en: Early in the Jianzhong era (780–783), learning that the court was fortifying Bianzhou, he plotted with Tian Yue, Liang Chongyi, and Li Weiyue to rebel together.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, hearing that Bian Prefecture was being fortified, he joined Tian Yue, Liang Chongyi, and Li Weiyue in a concerted rebellion.

units.zh: 自屯濟陰，陳兵按習，益師徐州以扼江、淮。
units.en: He camped at Jiyin, drilled his armies in the field, and reinforced Xuzhou to block the Yangzi and Huai routes.
units.literal: He himself encamped at Jiyin, arrayed troops for drill and review, and reinforced Xuzhou to choke the Yangzi and Huai.

units.zh: 天子於是改運道，檄天下兵為守備，河南騷然。
units.en: The emperor rerouted the grain transports and called up troops empire-wide; the Henan region erupted in alarm.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven thereupon altered the transport routes and issued orders to armies throughout the realm for defense; Henan was thrown into turmoil.

units.zh: 會發疽死，年四十九。
units.en: He died of an abscess at the age of forty-nine.
units.literal: He happened to die of a carbuncle; he was forty-nine years old.

units.zh: 興元初，納順命，詔贈太尉。
units.en: Early in the Xingyuan era (784), Li Na submitted to the throne, and the court posthumously honored Zhengji as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Xingyuan era, Na submitted to orders; an edict posthumously for Zhengji granted Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 納，少時為奉禮郎，將兵防秋。
units.en: Li Na had begun as a ceremonial attendant in his youth and later commanded troops on autumn frontier duty.
units.literal: Na, in his youth, was a ceremonial attendant and led troops for autumn defense.

units.zh: 代宗召見，擢殿中丞，賜金紫。
units.en: Emperor Daizong received him at court, promoted him to palace censor, and awarded the gold-and-purple regalia of high rank.
units.literal: Emperor Daizong summoned him for audience, promoted him to palace censor, and bestowed gold-purple insignia.

units.zh: 入朝，擢兼侍御史。
units.en: When he came to the capital he was further named concurrent investigating censor.
units.literal: On entering court he was further promoted to concurrent investigating censor.

units.zh: 正己署為淄、青二州刺史，又為行軍司馬，濮、徐、兗、沂、海留後，進御史大夫。
units.en: Zhengji named him prefect of Zi and Qing, then field marshal and acting governor of Pu, Xu, Yan, Yi, and Hai, and eventually promoted him to chief censor.
units.literal: Zhengji appointed him prefect of the two prefectures Zi and Qing, then campaigning marshal, acting governor of Pu, Xu, Yan, Yi, and Hai, and advanced him to censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 正己死，秘喪不發，以兵會田悅於濮陽。
units.en: When Zhengji died, Na kept the death secret and marched to join Tian Yue at Puyang.
units.literal: When Zhengji died, Na concealed the death and did not announce mourning, and with troops joined Tian Yue at Puyang.

units.zh: 馬燧方擊悅，納使大將衛俊救之，為燧所破略盡，收洹水。
units.en: Ma Sui was pressing Tian Yue hard; Na sent his general Wei Jun to the rescue, but Sui shattered the relief force and retook Huanshui.
units.literal: Ma Sui was then attacking Yue; Na sent the great general Wei Jun to rescue him, but Sui routed them nearly to annihilation and recovered Huanshui.

units.zh: 德宗詔諸軍合討，其從父洧以徐州歸，大將李士真以德州、李長卿以棣州送款，納恚洧背己，且徐險集，悉兵攻洧。
units.en: Emperor Dezong ordered a general assault; Na's clansman Li Wei defected with Xuzhou, while Li Shizhen surrendered Dezhou and Li Changqing surrendered Di Prefecture. Furious at Wei's betrayal and mindful of Xuzhou's rugged defenses, Na threw his entire army against him.
units.literal: Emperor Dezong ordered the armies to join in a combined attack; his cousin by the father's line Wei surrendered Xuzhou, the great general Li Shizhen offered De Prefecture, and Li Changqing offered Di Prefecture. Na resented Wei for turning against him, and because Xu was rugged and well defended, he sent all his troops against Wei.

units.zh: 帝命宣武、劉玄佐督諸軍進援，大破其兵。
units.en: The emperor ordered the Xuanwu army and Liu Xuanzuo to direct the relief and inflicted a crushing defeat on Na's army.
units.literal: The emperor ordered Xuanwu and Liu Xuanzuo to direct the armies in advance relief and greatly defeated Na's forces.

units.zh: 納還濮陽，玄佐進圍之，殘其郛。
units.en: Na fell back to Puyang, where Xuanzuo besieged him and tore down the outer ramparts.
units.literal: Na returned to Puyang; Xuanzuo advanced to besiege it and ravaged its outer walls.

units.zh: 納登陴見玄佐，泣且悔，遣判官房說與子弟質京師，因玄佐謝罪。
units.en: Na climbed the battlements to face Xuanzuo in tears and remorse, sent his secretary Fang Yue and his sons to the capital as hostages, and sued for pardon through Xuanzuo.
units.literal: Na ascended the wall to meet Xuanzuo, weeping and repenting; he sent his aide Fang Yue and his sons and younger brothers as hostages to the capital and, through Xuanzuo, begged forgiveness.

units.zh: 時中人宋鳳朝以納窮，欲立功，建不可赦，帝乃械說等禁中。
units.en: The eunuch Song Fengchao, seeing Na at bay, urged that he must not be forgiven and the emperor had Fang Yue and the hostages clapped in irons within the palace.
units.literal: At that time the eunuch Song Fengchao, seeing Na cornered, wished to win merit and urged that he must not be pardoned; the emperor thereupon shackled Fang Yue and the others in the palace.

units.zh: 納於是還鄆，與悅、李希烈、朱滔、王武俊連和，自稱齊王，置百官。
units.en: Na withdrew to Yunzhou, joined forces with Yue, Li Xilie, Zhu Tao, and Wang Wujun, proclaimed himself King of Qi, and installed a full court of officials.
units.literal: Na thereupon returned to Yun, allied with Yue, Li Xilie, Zhu Tao, and Wang Wujun, styled himself King of Qi, and established the full bureaucracy.

units.zh: 興元初，帝下詔罪己，納復歸命，授檢校工部尚書，復平盧帥節，賜鐵券，又同中書門下平章事，封隴西郡王。
units.en: When the emperor issued his famous self-reproach edict early in the Xingyuan era, Na submitted again; he was named acting Minister of Works, restored as military governor of Pinglu, given an iron covenant of mercy, made honorary Grand Councillor, and enfeoffed Prince of Longxi.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan, the emperor issued a self-reproach edict; Na again submitted to orders, was appointed acting Minister of Works, restored to command of Pinglu, granted an iron covenant, again made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Prince of Longxi commandery.

units.zh: 希烈圍陳州，納會諸軍破之城下，加檢校司空，實封五百戶，進檢校司徒。
units.en: When Li Xilie besieged Chenzhou, Na joined the relief armies and routed him below the walls; he was promoted to acting Minister of Works with a fief of five hundred households, then to acting Grand Mentor.
units.literal: Xilie besieged Chen Prefecture; Na joined the armies and defeated him beneath the walls, was added acting Minister of Works, granted a substantive fief of five hundred households, and advanced to acting Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 死年三十四，贈太傅。
units.en: He died at thirty-four and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He died at the age of thirty-four; posthumously he was granted Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 子師古、師道。
units.en: His sons were Li Shigu and Li Shidao.
units.literal: His sons were Shigu and Shidao.

units.zh: 師古，以蔭累署青州刺史。
units.en: Li Shigu, through hereditary privilege, held the post of Qingzhou prefect.
units.literal: Shigu, through successive yin privileges, was appointed prefect of Qing Prefecture.

units.zh: 納死，軍中請嗣帥，詔起為右金吾衛大將軍、本軍節度使。
units.en: After Na's death the troops demanded Shigu as successor; an edict recalled him from mourning as general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and military governor of the circuit.
units.literal: When Na died, the army requested a successor commander; an edict recalled him to serve as great general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and military governor of his own army.

units.zh: 初，棣州有蛤𧊶|虫朵鹽池，歲產鹽數十萬斛。
units.en: Di Prefecture had long possessed the Hadu salt flats, which yielded several hundred thousand bushels of salt annually.
units.literal: Earlier, Di Prefecture had the Hadu salt pans, producing several hundred thousand hu of salt each year.

units.zh: 李長卿以州入朱滔，獨蛤𧊶|虫朵為納所據以專利。
units.en: When Li Changqing surrendered the prefecture to Zhu Tao, Na alone kept Hadu and monopolized its salt profits.
units.literal: Li Changqing surrendered the prefecture to Zhu Tao; only Hadu remained held by Na for his exclusive profit.

units.zh: 後德、棣入王武俊，納乃築壘德州南，跨河以守蛤𧊶|虫朵，謂之三汊，通魏博以交田緒，盜掠德州，武俊患之。
units.en: When De and Di later fell to Wang Wujun, Na built a fortified camp south of Dezhou astride the river to hold Hadu—the "Three Forks"—linked with Weibo through Tian Xu, and raided Dezhou, to Wujun's great annoyance.
units.literal: Later De and Di came under Wang Wujun; Na then built a fort south of De Prefecture, spanning the river to guard Hadu, called it the Three Forks, opened contact with Weibo to ally with Tian Xu, and raided De Prefecture, to Wujun's distress.

units.zh: 師古殆襲，武俊易其弱，且納時將無在，乃率兵取蛤𧊶|虫朵、三汊。
units.en: With Shigu gravely ill, Wujun judged him an easy mark; Na's veteran commanders were gone as well, so Wujun marched and seized Hadu and the Three Forks.
units.literal: Shigu was near death; Wujun regarded him as weak, and moreover none of Na's seasoned generals remained, so he led troops to take Hadu and the Three Forks.

units.zh: 師古使趙鎬拒戰，武俊子士清兵先濟滴河，會營中火起，士大噪不敢前。
units.en: Shigu sent Zhao Hao to hold them off; Wujun's son Wang Shiqing crossed the Di River first, but a fire erupted in camp, the men panicked, and they would not press the attack.
units.literal: Shigu sent Zhao Hao to resist; Wujun's son Shiqing's troops first crossed the Di River, but when fire broke out in the camp the soldiers clamored and dared not advance.

units.zh: 德宗遣使者諭武俊罷兵。
units.en: Emperor Dezong sent envoys ordering Wujun to stand down.
units.literal: Emperor Dezong sent envoys instructing Wujun to cease hostilities.

units.zh: 師古亦隳三汊聽命。
units.en: Shigu likewise dismantled the Three Forks fort and submitted to the court's command.
units.literal: Shigu also demolished the Three Forks and obeyed orders.

units.zh: 嘗怒其僚獨孤造，使奏事京師，遣大將王濟縊殺之。
units.en: Once, furious at his aide Dugu Zao, he sent him to the capital on official business and had his general Wang Ji strangle him on the road.
units.literal: Once, enraged at his subordinate Dugu Zao, he sent him to report at the capital and dispatched the great general Wang Ji to strangle him.

units.zh: 貞元末，與杜佑、李欒皆得封妾媵以國為夫人，進同中書門下平章事。
units.en: Late in the Zhenyuan era he joined Du You and Li Luan in the unprecedented privilege of ennobling concubines as state ladies, and was promoted to honorary Grand Councillor.
units.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, he, together with Du You and Li Luan, all obtained the privilege of ennobling concubines as state ladies; he was advanced to co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

units.zh: 德宗崩，哀使未至，義成節度使李元素騰遺詔示之。
units.en: When Dezong died, before the official mourning envoy arrived, the Yicheng governor Li Yuansu showed him the late emperor's testament.
units.literal: When Dezong died, the mourning envoy had not yet arrived; the Yicheng military governor Li Yuansu displayed the testamentary edict to him.

units.zh: 師古幸國喪，欲攻掠州縣，即集將士告：「元素偽作遺詔，豈欲反邪？
units.en: Shigu welcomed the imperial bereavement and prepared to raid neighboring prefectures; he assembled his commanders and declared, "Yuansu has forged the testament—surely he means to rebel?
units.literal: Shigu rejoiced at the national mourning and wished to attack and plunder prefectures and counties; he immediately gathered officers and troops and announced: "Yuansu forged the testamentary edict—does he not intend rebellion?

units.zh: 不可不討！」
units.en: We cannot fail to punish him!"
units.literal: He must be punished!"

units.zh: 執使者，名討元素，勒兵出次，聞順宗立，乃罷。
units.en: He detained the envoy, proclaimed a punitive expedition against Yuansu, and marched his army out—only to stand down when word came that Shunzong had succeeded to the throne.
units.literal: He seized the envoy, named a campaign to punish Yuansu, and marshaled troops to advance; hearing that Shunzong had ascended, he then desisted.

units.zh: 累加檢校司徒、兼侍中。
units.en: He was repeatedly promoted, ultimately to acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to acting Grand Mentor and concurrent Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 元和初卒，贈太傅。
units.en: He died early in the Yuanhe era (806–820) and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He died at the beginning of the Yuanhe era; posthumously he was granted Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 師道，異母弟也。
units.en: Li Shidao was his younger half-brother.
units.literal: Shidao was a younger brother by a different mother.

units.zh: 師古嘗曰：「是不更民間疾苦，要令知衣食所從。」
units.en: Shigu once remarked, "He has never known the people's hardships; he ought to learn where food and clothing come from."
units.literal: Shigu once said: "This one has not experienced the people's hardships; he must be made to know whence food and clothing come."

units.zh: 乃署知密州。
units.en: With that he sent him to serve as acting prefect of Mizhou.
units.literal: He therefore appointed him to administer Mi Prefecture.

units.zh: 師古病，召親近高沐、李公度等曰：「即我不諱，欲以誰嗣？」
units.en: As Shigu lay dying he called in his confidants Gao Mu and Li Gongdu and asked, "When I am gone, whom should succeed me?"
units.literal: When Shigu fell ill, he summoned his intimates Gao Mu, Li Gongdu, and others and said: "When I am gone, whom do you wish to succeed me?"

units.zh: 二人未對。
units.en: The two men did not reply.
units.literal: The two did not answer.

units.zh: 師古曰：「豈以人情屬師道邪？
units.en: Shigu said, "Are you inclined toward Shidao out of mere affection?
units.literal: Shigu said: "Would you entrust it to Shidao out of personal feeling?

units.zh: 彼不服戎，以技自尚，慮覆吾宗，公等審計之。」
units.en: He has no taste for soldiering, prides himself on petty talents, and I fear he will ruin our line—you must judge this carefully."
units.literal: He is unaccustomed to arms, prides himself on skills, and I fear he will overturn our house—you must weigh this carefully."

units.zh: 及死，沐、公度與家奴卒立之，而請於朝。
units.en: After his death, Gao Mu and Li Gongdu, with the household guard, installed Shidao and petitioned the throne for confirmation.
units.literal: When he died, Mu, Gongdu, and household slaves and soldiers installed him and petitioned the court.

units.zh: 於是制書久不下，師道謀裒兵守境，沐爭止，更上書奉兩稅，守鹽法，請吏朝廷。
units.en: When the appointment edict was slow in coming, Shidao prepared to mobilize and hold the borders; Gao Mu dissuaded him and he memorialized anew, pledging the two-tax levy, observance of salt regulations, and acceptance of court-appointed officials.
units.literal: Thereupon the appointment edict was long in coming; Shidao planned to gather troops and guard the borders, but Mu argued and stopped him; he again memorialized offering the two-tax system, observing salt laws, and requesting officials from the court.

units.zh: 宰相杜黃裳欲橈削其權，而憲宗方誅劉辟，未皇東討，故命建王審領節度大使，而以師道知留後。
units.en: Chief Minister Du Huangchang meant to curb his power, but Xianzong was still crushing Liu Pi in the west and could not yet march east; he therefore named Prince Shen of Jian nominal military commissioner while Shidao served as acting governor.
units.literal: The chief minister Du Huangchang wished to pare away his power, but Emperor Xianzong was just executing Liu Pi and had no leisure to campaign east; therefore he ordered the Prince of Jian, Shen, to take nominal command as military commissioner, while Shidao was made acting governor.

units.zh: 歲中，加檢校工部尚書，為副大使。
units.en: Within the year he was named acting Minister of Works and deputy commissioner.
units.literal: Within the year he was added acting Minister of Works as deputy commissioner.

units.zh: 自正己以來，雖外奉王命，而嘯引亡叛，有得罪於朝者厚納之。
units.en: Since Zhengji's day the family had outwardly obeyed the throne while sheltering fugitives and rebels, richly rewarding anyone the court had condemned.
units.literal: From Zhengji onward, though outwardly they obeyed imperial orders, they gathered and harbored fugitives and rebels; those who had offended the court they richly received.

units.zh: 以嚴法持下，凡所付遣，必質其妻子；
units.en: They ruled subordinates by terror: every agent sent on a mission had his wife and children held hostage;
units.literal: With harsh law they controlled subordinates; for every commission they gave, they necessarily took the men's wives and children as hostages;

units.zh: 有謀順者，類夷其家。
units.en: anyone who contemplated defecting to the court saw his entire family wiped out.
units.literal: those who plotted submission were generally exterminated root and branch.

units.zh: 以故能脅汙士眾，傳三世云。
units.en: Thus they cowed their officers and men and held power through three generations.
units.literal: Thus they could coerce and defile officers and troops, passing through three generations, it is said.

units.zh: 帝討蔡，詔興諸道兵而不及鄆，師道選卒二千抵壽春，陽言為王師助，實欲援蔡也。
units.en: When the emperor campaigned against Cai, he mobilized the circuits but omitted Yun; Shidao sent two thousand elite troops to Shouchun, claiming to reinforce the imperial armies while in fact aiming to aid Cai.
units.literal: The emperor attacked Cai; he ordered armies of the circuits to rise but did not include Yun; Shidao selected two thousand picked troops to reach Shouchun, openly claiming to aid the imperial armies but in truth intending to rescue Cai.

units.zh: 亡命少年為師道計曰：「河陰者，江、淮委輸，河南，帝都，請燒河陰敖庫，募洛壯士劫宮闕，即朝廷救腹心疾，此解蔡一奇也。」
units.en: An outlaw youth proposed to Shidao: "Heyin is the depot for Yangzi-Huai grain; Henan holds the capital. Burn the Heyin treasury, recruit bravos from Luoyang to storm the palace—the court will turn to save its heartland, and Cai's siege will be broken."
units.literal: A desperate youth devised a plan for Shidao, saying: "Heyin is where the Yangzi and Huai consign their transport; Henan is the imperial capital region. Please burn the Heyin granary treasury, recruit stalwart men of Luoyang to seize the palace gates—then the court will rush to save its vitals, and this is one stratagem to relieve Cai."

units.zh: 師道乃遣客燒河陰漕院錢三十萬緡，米數萬斛，倉百餘區。
units.en: Shidao sent agents who burned the Heyin transport depot—three hundred thousand strings in cash, tens of thousands of bushels of grain, and more than a hundred warehouses.
units.literal: Shidao then sent agents to burn the Heyin transport depot: cash to the value of three hundred thousand strings, several tens of thousands of hu of grain, and more than a hundred storehouses.

units.zh: 又有說師道曰：「上雖志討蔡，謀皆出宰相，而武元衡得君，願為袁盎事，後宰相必懼，請罷兵，是不用師，蔡圍解矣。」
units.en: Another adviser told Shidao: "The emperor means to crush Cai, but strategy rests with the chief ministers, and Wu Yuanheng has his ear. Do as Yuan Ang did—strike down the minister the emperor trusts; the court will panic and sue for peace, the armies will stand down, and Cai will be saved."
units.literal: Another urged Shidao, saying: "Although the emperor is resolved to attack Cai, the plans all come from the chief ministers, and Wu Yuanheng has the ruler's ear. I wish to do as Yuan Ang did; afterward the chief ministers will be afraid and beg to cease troops—then armies will not be used, and the siege of Cai will be lifted."

units.zh: 乃使人殺元衡，傷裴度。
units.en: He sent assassins who killed Wu Yuanheng and wounded Pei Du.
units.literal: He then sent men to kill Yuanheng and wound Pei Du.

units.zh: 初，師道置邸東都，多買田伊闕、陸渾間，以舍山棚，遣將訾嘉珍、門察部分之，嵩山浮屠圓靜為之謀。
units.en: Earlier Shidao had set up a residence in Luoyang and bought land between Yique and Luhun to lodge his "mountain shed" agents, assigning the generals Zi Jiazhen and Men Cha to organize them; the Mount Song monk Yuanjing masterminded the plot.
units.literal: Earlier, Shidao established a lodge in the eastern capital, bought much land between Yique and Luhun to house mountain sheds, and sent the generals Zi Jiazhen and Men Cha to apportion it; the Songshan monk Yuanjing plotted for him.

units.zh: 元和十年，大饗士邸中，椎牛釃酒，既衷甲矣，其徒白官發之。
units.en: In Yuanhe 10 (815) he held a great feast at the lodge, slaughtered cattle, and broached wine; his men were already armored underneath when one of them betrayed the plot to the authorities.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, he feasted his men greatly in the lodge, slaughtered oxen and strained wine; they had already donned armor beneath their robes when one of the band informed the authorities.

units.zh: 留守呂元膺以兵掩邸，賊突出，轉略畿部，入山中數月，奪山棚所市，山棚怒，道官軍襲擊，盡殺之。
units.en: Luoyang defender Lü Yuanying stormed the lodge; the rebels broke out, raided the capital outskirts, and hid in the hills for months, robbing the mountain sheds' markets. The sheds, furious, guided imperial troops to the hideout and wiped them out.
units.literal: The Luoyang defender Lü Yuanying attacked the lodge with troops; the bandits broke out, turned to plunder the capital districts, and entered the mountains for several months, seizing what the mountain sheds had marketed; the sheds were enraged and guided government troops in an assault, killing them all.

units.zh: 圓靜者，年八十餘，嘗為史思明將，驍悍絕倫。
units.en: Yuanjing was over eighty, a former general under Shi Siming, and accounted the fiercest fighter of his day.
units.literal: Yuanjing was more than eighty years old and had once been a general of Shi Siming; in valor and fierceness he was without peer.

units.zh: 既執，力士椎其脛，不能折，罵曰：「豎子，折人腳且不能，乃曰健兒！」
units.en: Once captured, brawny guards battered his shins without breaking them; he swore, "You pups can't even break a man's leg and call yourselves warriors!"
units.literal: Once seized, strongmen struck his shins but could not break them; he cursed, saying: "Whelps! You cannot even break a man's leg and yet call yourselves stalwarts!"

units.zh: 因自置其足折之。
units.en: He set his own foot against a post and snapped the bone himself.
units.literal: He then set his own foot and broke it.

units.zh: 且死，嘆曰：「敗吾事，不得見洛城流血！」
units.en: Facing execution he sighed, "You have ruined everything—I shall never see Luoyang awash in blood!"
units.literal: As he was about to die, he sighed: "You have ruined my affair—I shall not see Luoyang's streets run with blood!"

units.zh: 於時，留守、防禦將、都亭驛史數十人，皆陰受師道署職，使為诇察，故無知者。
units.en: Dozens of Luoyang officials—the defender, garrison commanders, and post-house clerks—had all been secretly on Shidao's payroll as spies, which is why the plot went undetected.
units.literal: At that time, several tens of the defender, defense generals, and Duting post clerks had all secretly received appointments from Shidao and served as spies, so none knew.

units.zh: 及窮治，嘉珍、察乃害武元衡者。
units.en: Under full investigation it emerged that Jiazhen and Cha were Yuanheng's assassins.
units.literal: When the case was pursued to the end, Jiazhen and Cha were those who had killed Wu Yuanheng.

units.zh: 鹽鐵使王播又得嘉珍所藏弓材五千，並斷建陵戟四十七。
units.en: Salt Commissioner Wang Bo also seized five thousand bow staves from Jiazhen's cache and forty-seven halberds illegally cut from the Jianling imperial arsenal.
units.literal: The salt and iron commissioner Wang Bo further recovered five thousand bow staves hoarded by Jiazhen, together with forty-seven halberds cut from Jianling.

units.zh: 始，師道欲知元濟虛實，使劉晏平間道走淮西。
units.en: Earlier Shidao had wanted intelligence on Wu Yuanji and sent Liu Yanping by a back road into Huaixi.
units.literal: At first Shidao wished to learn the true state of Wu Yuanji and sent Liu Yanping by a secret route to Huaixi.

units.zh: 元濟日與宴，厚結歡。
units.en: Yuanji wined and dined him daily and won his warm friendship.
units.literal: Yuanji feasted with him daily and bound him in deep friendship.

units.zh: 晏平歸，以為元濟暴師數萬，而晏然居內，與妻妾戲博，必敗之道也。
units.en: On his return Yanping reported that Yuanji kept tens of thousands in the field yet lounged inside with his wives, gambling—certainly the path to ruin.
units.literal: Yanping returned and judged that Yuanji exposed tens of thousands of troops while calmly dwelling within, gaming with wives and concubines—this was surely the way to defeat.

units.zh: 師道本倚蔡為重，聞之怒，乃以它事殺晏平。
units.en: Shidao had counted on Cai's strength; enraged by the report, he had Yanping executed on a trumped-up charge.
units.literal: Shidao had relied on Cai for his weight; hearing this he was enraged and killed Yanping on another pretext.

units.zh: 及聞李光顏拔淩雲柵，始大懼，遣使歸順，帝重分兵支兩寇，故命給事中柳公綽慰撫之，加檢校司空。
units.en: When Li Guangyan captured the Lingyun stockade, Shidao was thoroughly alarmed and sent envoys to surrender; the emperor, stretched between two fronts, dispatched Liu Gongchuo to reassure him and named him acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: When he heard that Li Guangyan had taken the Lingyun stockade, he was greatly afraid for the first time, sent envoys to submit, and the emperor, heavily dividing troops to meet two enemies, therefore ordered the Supervising Secretary Liu Gongchuo to console him and added acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 蔡平，又遣比部員外郎張宿諷令割地質子。
units.en: After Cai fell, the court sent Review Bureau Vice-Director Zhang Su to press him to surrender territory and send a hostage son.
units.literal: When Cai was pacified, he again sent the bureau of review vice-director Zhang Su to urge him to cede territory and send a hostage.

units.zh: 宿謂曰：「公今歸國為宗姓，以尊卑論之，上叔父矣，不屈一也；
units.en: Zhang Su told him: "You have rejoined the imperial clan; by rank the emperor is your uncle—no need to humble yourself, first point;
units.literal: Su said to him: "You now return to the state as a clansman; in terms of senior and junior, the emperor is your uncle—no need to bow, first point;

units.zh: 以十二州事三百餘州天子，北面稱藩，不屈二也；
units.en: twelve prefectures against the Son of Heaven's three hundred—you are a vassal facing north—no need to bow, second point;
units.literal: with twelve prefectures serving a Son of Heaven of more than three hundred prefectures, you face north as a vassal—no need to bow, second point;

units.zh: 以五十年傳爵，臣二百年天子，不屈三也。
units.en: fifty years your family has held its fief, two centuries the Tang have ruled—no need to bow, third point.
units.literal: with fifty years of transmitted fief, you are subject to a two-hundred-year Son of Heaven—no need to bow, third point.

units.zh: 今反狀己暴，上猶許內省，宜遣子入宿衛，割地以贖罪。」
units.en: Your rebellion is exposed, yet the emperor still offers you a way back—send your son to the capital guard and cede land to atone."
units.literal: Now your rebellion is already exposed, yet the emperor still permits inward reflection; you should send your son to serve in the palace guard and cede territory to atone for guilt."

units.zh: 師道乃納三州，遣子弘方入侍。
units.en: Shidao surrendered three prefectures and sent his son Li Hongfang to the capital as hostage.
units.literal: Shidao then surrendered three prefectures and sent his son Hongfang to attend at court.

units.zh: 宿既還，師道中悔，召諸將議，皆曰：「蔡數州，戰三四年乃克，公今十二州，何所虞？」
units.en: After Zhang Su left, Shidao wavered and called his generals in council; all said, "Cai was only a few prefectures and took three or four years to crush—you hold twelve; what have you to fear?"
units.literal: When Su had returned, Shidao midway repented; he summoned the generals to deliberate, and all said: "Cai had only a few prefectures and took three or four years to conquer—my lord now has twelve prefectures, what is there to fear?"

units.zh: 大將崔承度獨進曰：「公初不示諸將腹心，而今委以兵，此皆嗜利者，朝廷以一漿十餅誘之去矣。」
units.en: Only General Cui Chengdu objected: "You never trusted your commanders with your true plans, yet now you give them armies—these are mercenaries; the court will buy them off with a bowl of gruel for ten cakes."
units.literal: The great general Cui Chengdu alone advanced and said: "My lord at first did not show the generals your inner mind, yet now you entrust them with troops—these are all men who crave profit; the court will lure them away with one bowl of gruel for ten cakes."

units.zh: 師道恚，遣承度詣京師，戒候吏時其還斬之。
units.en: Shidao, furious, sent Chengdu to the capital and ordered the border guards to execute him on his return.
units.literal: Shidao was furious and sent Chengdu to the capital, instructing the border officers to behead him when he returned.

units.zh: 承度待命客省，不敢還。
units.en: Chengdu waited in the capital guest office and dared not go home.
units.literal: Chengdu awaited orders in the guest-reception office and did not dare return.

units.zh: 帝以其負約，用左散騎常侍李遜喻旨。
units.en: The emperor, angered by his breach of faith, sent Left Cavalry Attendant Li Xun to deliver the court's message.
units.literal: Because he had broken his covenant, the emperor employed the Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Li Xun to convey the imperial intent.

units.zh: 既至，師道嚴兵以見，遜讓曰：「前已約，而今背之，何也？
units.en: On arrival Shidao received him under arms; Xun protested, "We had a pact—why have you broken it?
units.literal: When he arrived, Shidao received him with troops drawn up in formation; Xun remonstrated, saying: "We had an agreement before—why do you go back on it now?

units.zh: 願得要言奏天子。」
units.en: I need your clear answer to carry back to the emperor."
units.literal: I wish to obtain your essential words to report to the Son of Heaven."

units.zh: 師道許之，然懦暗不自決。
units.en: Shidao agreed in words but was too timid and indecisive to act.
units.literal: Shidao agreed, yet he was timid and dull and could not decide for himself.

units.zh: 私奴婢媼爭言：「先司徒土地，奈何一旦割之？
units.en: His household women and old nurses clamored, "The former Grand Mentor's lands—how can you surrender them in a day?
units.literal: His private slave women and old nurses argued among themselves: "The former Grand Mentor's lands—how can we cut them off all at once?

units.zh: 今不獻三州，不過戰耳，即不勝，割地未晚。」
units.en: Refuse the three prefectures and we fight; if we lose, we can still cede land later."
units.literal: If we do not surrender the three prefectures now, it is no more than fighting; even if we do not win, ceding territory will not be too late."

units.zh: 師道乃上書，以軍不協為解。
units.en: Shidao memorialized the throne, blaming his troops' refusal to comply.
units.literal: Shidao then memorialized, offering as his excuse that the army would not agree.

units.zh: 帝怒，下詔削其官，詔諸軍進討。
units.en: The emperor stripped his titles by edict and ordered a general offensive.
units.literal: The emperor was enraged, issued an edict stripping his offices, and ordered the armies to advance in attack.

units.zh: 武寧節度使李願使將王智興破其眾，斬二千級，獲馬牛四千，略地至平陰。
units.en: Li Yuan of Wuning sent Wang Zhixing to crush Shidao's army—two thousand heads, four thousand horses and oxen—and pushed the frontier to Pingyin.
units.literal: The Wuning military governor Li Yuan sent the general Wang Zhixing to rout his forces, beheading two thousand, capturing four thousand horses and cattle, and seizing territory as far as Pingyin.

units.zh: 橫海節度使鄭權戰福城，斬五百級。
units.en: Zheng Quan of Heng-Hai fought at Fucheng and took five hundred heads.
units.literal: The Heng-Hai military governor Zheng Quan fought at Fucheng and beheaded five hundred.

units.zh: 武寧將李祐戰魚臺，敗之。
units.en: Li You of Wuning defeated them at Yutai.
units.literal: The Wuning general Li You fought at Yutai and defeated them.

units.zh: 宣武節度使韓弘拔考城。
units.en: Han Hong of Xuanwu captured Kaocheng.
units.literal: The Xuanwu military governor Han Hong took Kaocheng.

units.zh: 淮南節度使李夷簡命李聽趨海州，下沭湯、朐山，進戍東海。
units.en: Li Yijian of Huainan sent Li Ting to seize Hai Prefecture, Shuyang, and Qushan, and garrison the Eastern Sea coast.
units.literal: The Huainan military governor Li Yijian ordered Li Ting to hurry to Hai Prefecture, take Shuyang and Qushan, and advance to garrison the Eastern Sea.

units.zh: 魏博節度使田弘正身將兵自陽劉濟河，拒鄆四十里而營，再接戰，破三萬眾，禽三千人。
units.en: Tian Hongzheng of Weibo crossed from Yangliu, camped forty li from Yunzhou, routed thirty thousand men, and took three thousand prisoners.
units.literal: The Weibo military governor Tian Hongzheng personally led troops from Yangliu across the river, encamped forty li from Yun, fought again, routed thirty thousand, and captured three thousand.

units.zh: 陳許節度使李光顏攻濮陽，收鬥門、杜莊二屯。
units.en: Li Guangyan of Chenxu attacked Puyang and seized the stockades at Doumen and Duzhuang.
units.literal: The Chenxu military governor Li Guangyan attacked Puyang and recovered the two stockades Doumen and Duzhuang.

units.zh: 弘正又戰東阿，殘其眾五萬。
units.en: Hongzheng fought again at Dong'e and shattered fifty thousand of the enemy.
units.literal: Hongzheng again fought at Dong'e and mauled fifty thousand of their troops.

units.zh: 師道每聞敗，輒悸成疾，及李祐取金鄉，左右莫敢白。
units.en: Each defeat sent Shidao into trembling fits; when Li You captured Jinxiang, his attendants dared not tell him.
units.literal: Whenever Shidao heard of defeat he would palpitate into illness; when Li You took Jinxiang, none of those around him dared inform him.

units.zh: 初，遣大將劉悟屯陽谷，當魏博軍，疑其逗留，悟懼不免，引兵反攻城。
units.en: He had posted Liu Wu at Yanggu to block Weibo; fearing execution for delay, Wu turned his army against Yunzhou.
units.literal: Earlier he had sent the great general Liu Wu to garrison Yanggu against the Weibo army; suspecting delay, Wu feared he would not escape punishment and led troops back to storm the city.

units.zh: 師道晨起聞之，白其嫂裴曰：「悟兵反，將求為民，守墳墓。」
units.en: Shidao learned of it at dawn and told his sister-in-law Lady Pei, "Wu has mutinied; he means to become a commoner and tend our graves."
units.literal: Shidao rose early and heard of it; he told his sister-in-law Lady Pei: "Wu's troops have rebelled; he will seek to become a commoner and guard the graves."

units.zh: 即與弘方匿混間，兵就禽之。
units.en: He and Hongfang hid in a latrine and were captured on the spot.
units.literal: He and Hongfang at once hid in a privy; the soldiers came and seized them.

units.zh: 師道請見悟，不許，復請送京師，悟使謂曰：「司空今為囚，何面目見天子！」
units.en: Shidao begged to see Wu and then to be sent to the capital; Wu's messenger replied, "You are a prisoner—what face have you to show the emperor?"
units.literal: Shidao asked to see Wu but was not permitted; he again asked to be sent to the capital; Wu had someone tell him: "The Minister of Works is now a prisoner—what face has he to see the Son of Heaven!"

units.zh: 猶俯仰祈哀，弘方曰：「不若速死！」
units.en: He still groveled in pleas; Hongfang said, "Better die at once!"
units.literal: He still bowed and pleaded; Hongfang said: "Better to die quickly!"

units.zh: 乃並斬之，傳首京師。
units.en: Both were beheaded and their heads sent to Chang'an.
units.literal: They were then both beheaded, and their heads were sent to the capital.

units.zh: 棄其屍，無敢收視者，有士英秀為殯城左。
units.en: Their bodies lay unclaimed until the gentleman Yingxiu gave them burial outside the west gate.
units.literal: Their corpses were abandoned; none dared to attend them; a refined gentleman, Yingxiu, buried them outside the left of the city.

units.zh: 馬至，以士禮更葬。
units.en: When Ma Zhi came, he reburied them with full ceremonial honors.
units.literal: When Ma Zhi arrived, he reburied them with the rites due a gentleman.

units.zh: 初，師古見劉悟，曰：「後必貴，然敗吾家者此人也。」
units.en: Long before, Shigu had met Liu Wu and said, "He will rise high—but he will be the ruin of our house."
units.literal: Earlier, when Shigu saw Liu Wu, he said: "Later he will surely rise high, yet the one who will ruin our house is this man."

units.zh: 田弘正之度河也，禽其將夏侯澄等四十七人，有詔悉赦之，給繒絮，還隸魏博、義成軍，父母在欲還者優遣，賊皆感慰相告，由是悟得行其謀。
units.en: When Tian Hongzheng crossed the river he captured forty-seven officers including Xiahou Cheng; the court pardoned them all, clothed them, and sent them back to Weibo and Yicheng—with generous leave for those whose parents wanted them home. The rebels were deeply moved, which is how Wu won them to his mutiny.
units.literal: When Tian Hongzheng crossed the river, he captured their generals Xiahou Cheng and forty-seven others; an edict pardoned them all, gave silk and cotton, and returned them to Weibo and Yicheng armies; those whose parents wished them home were generously sent back; the rebels were all moved and comforted one another, and thus Wu was able to carry out his plot.

units.zh: 師道首傳弘正營，召澄驗之，澄舐目中塵，號絕良久。
units.en: Shidao's head reached Hongzheng's camp; Cheng was called to identify it, wiped the dust from his eyes, and keened until he collapsed.
units.literal: Shidao's head was sent to Hongzheng's camp; Cheng was summoned to identify it; he licked the dust from his eyes and wailed until he nearly died.

units.zh: 悟素與師道妻魏亂，妄言鄭公征之裔，不死，沒入掖廷，它宗屬悉遠徙。
units.en: Wu had long feuded with Shidao's wife Lady Wei, who falsely claimed to be a survivor of the Zheng clan purged into the palace women's quarters; the rest of the Li kindred were exiled.
units.literal: Wu had long been on bad terms with Shidao's wife Lady Wei; she falsely claimed descent from Duke Zheng's campaign lineage, that she had not died but been taken into the palace women, and all other clansmen were exiled far away.

units.zh: 悟獨表師古子明安為朗州司戶參軍。
units.en: Wu alone petitioned to name Shigu's son Ming'an registrar at Langzhou.
units.literal: Wu alone memorialized to appoint Shigu's son Ming'an as registrar of Lang Prefecture.

units.zh: 親將王承慶，承宗弟也，師道以兄女妻之，潛約左右，欲因肄兵執師道，會悟入，出奔徐州，歸朝。
units.en: Wang Chengqing, a favored commander and younger brother of Chengzong, whom Shidao had married to his elder brother's daughter, had plotted with his men to arrest Shidao during maneuvers; when Wu stormed the city he fled to Xuzhou and defected to the court.
units.literal: The intimate general Wang Chengqing, younger brother of Chengzong, whom Shidao had married to his elder brother's daughter, secretly agreed with those close to him to seize Shidao during drill; when Wu entered the city he fled to Xuzhou and submitted to the court.

units.zh: 程日華，定州安喜人，始名華，德宗以其有功，益曰日華。
units.en: Cheng Rihua, a native of Anxi in Dingzhou, was originally named Hua; Emperor Dezong, honoring his service, enlarged his name to Rihua.
units.literal: Cheng Rihua was a man of Anxi in Ding Prefecture; his original name was Hua; Dezong, because of his merit, added the character Ri to make Rihua.

units.zh: 父元皓為安祿山帳下，偽署定州刺史，故日華籍本軍，為張孝忠牙將。
units.en: His father Yuanhao had served An Lushan as puppet prefect of Dingzhou; Rihua entered the home army and became a guard officer under Zhang Xiaozhong.
units.literal: His father Yuanhao had been in An Lushan's camp and was falsely appointed prefect of Ding Prefecture; therefore Rihua was registered in the native army and served as Zhang Xiaozhong's guard officer.

units.zh: 滄，故成德部州也，孝忠絕李惟嶽，德宗以滄畀義武。
units.en: Cangzhou had belonged to Chengde; when Xiaozhong broke with Li Weiyue, Dezong awarded it to Yiwu.
units.literal: Cang was formerly a prefecture of Chengde; Xiaozhong broke with Li Weiyue, and Dezong gave Cang to Yiwu.

units.zh: 前刺史李固烈與惟嶽姻屬，即牢守。
units.en: The outgoing prefect Li Gulie, Weiyue's kinsman by marriage, barricaded himself in the city.
units.literal: The former prefect Li Gulie was related by marriage to Weiyue and at once held the city fast.

units.zh: 孝忠令日華往喻之，固烈請還恒州。
units.en: Xiaozhong sent Rihua to reason with him; Gulie agreed to withdraw to Hengzhou.
units.literal: Xiaozhong ordered Rihua to go persuade him; Gulie asked to return to Heng Prefecture.

units.zh: 既治裝，悉帑以行，軍中怒曰：「馬瘠，士饑死，刺史不棄豪發恤吾急，今刮地以去，吾等何望？」
units.en: As he packed to leave with every coin he could carry, the troops raged: "Our horses are starved, our men dying of hunger, and the prefect won't spare a penny—now he strips the place bare. What hope is left for us?"
units.literal: When he had packed, he took all his wealth with him; the army raged, saying: "The horses are lean, the soldiers starving to death—the prefect will not spare a hair to relieve our distress, yet now he scrapes the land bare and leaves—what hope have we?"

units.zh: 遂共殺固烈，屠其家。
units.en: They killed Gulie and massacred his family.
units.literal: They then together killed Gulie and slaughtered his household.

units.zh: 日華驚匿床下，將士迎出之曰：「暴吾軍者已死，何畏而亡？」
units.en: Rihua hid under a bed in terror; the soldiers pulled him out, saying, "The man who wronged us is dead—why should you flee?"
units.literal: Rihua in alarm hid under a bed; officers and soldiers brought him out, saying: "He who wronged our army is dead—why fear and flee?"

units.zh: 共逼領州。
units.en: They pressed him to take command of the prefecture.
units.literal: Together they compelled him to take charge of the prefecture.

units.zh: 孝忠亦以日華寬厚，遂假以刺史。
units.en: Xiaozhong, impressed by Rihua's generous character, confirmed him as acting prefect.
units.literal: Xiaozhong also, because Rihua was generous and mild, thereupon provisionally appointed him prefect.

units.zh: 朱滔叛，兵屯河間，以故滄、定道阻不相聞。
units.en: When Zhu Tao rebelled and camped at Hejian, Cang and Ding were cut off from one another.
units.literal: Zhu Tao rebelled and stationed troops at Hejian; because of this the routes between Cang and Ding were blocked and they could not communicate.

units.zh: 滔及王武俊皆招日華，不納，即攻之。
units.en: Both Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun tried to win him over; he refused, and they attacked at once.
units.literal: Tao and Wang Wujun both recruited Rihua; he did not accept and they at once attacked him.

units.zh: 日華乘城自固。
units.en: Rihua manned the walls and held out.
units.literal: Rihua mounted the walls and held firm.

units.zh: 參軍事李宇謀曰：「城久圍，府兵不為援。
units.en: His aide Li Yu urged, "The siege drags on and Yiwu's army never comes.
units.literal: The staff officer Li Yu advised, saying: "The city has been long besieged and the circuit troops do not come to our aid.

units.zh: 今州十縣瀕海，有魚鹽利自給，此軍本號橫海，將軍能絕易定歸天子，自為一州，甲訓兵，利則出，無利則守，可亢盜喉襟。
units.en: Your ten coastal counties live on fish and salt; this command was once called Heng-Hai. Break with Yi and Ding, submit directly to the emperor as an independent circuit, train your army, strike when profit offers and hold when it does not—you can throttle the rebels' lifeline.
units.literal: Now the prefecture's ten counties border the sea and have fish and salt profits to sustain themselves; this army was originally called Heng-Hai. If the general can break with Yi and Ding and return to the Son of Heaven, establish himself as a separate prefecture, arm and train troops, advance when there is profit and hold when there is none, he can choke the rebels' throat.

units.zh: 君能用仆計，請至京師為天子言之。」
units.en: Adopt my plan and I will go to Chang'an and plead your case to the emperor."
units.literal: If my lord will use this plan of mine, I ask to go to the capital and speak to the Son of Heaven on his behalf."

units.zh: 日華謂然，乃遣宇西，帝果大喜，拜御史中丞、滄州刺史，復置橫海軍，即以為使，時建中三年也。
units.en: Rihua agreed and sent Yu west; the emperor was delighted, named him vice censor-in-chief and prefect of Cang, restored the Heng-Hai command, and made him its military governor in Jianzhong 3 (782).
units.literal: Rihua judged it right and sent Yu west; the emperor was indeed greatly pleased, appointed him vice censor-in-chief and prefect of Cang, restored the Heng-Hai army, and at once made him its commissioner—it was the third year of Jianzhong.

units.zh: 拜檢校工部尚書。
units.en: He was named acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: He was appointed acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 詔滄歲饋義武錢十二萬緡，糧數萬斛，以宇為判官。
units.en: The court ordered Cang to send Yiwu one hundred twenty thousand strings in cash and tens of thousands of bushels of grain yearly, with Yu as his chief aide.
units.literal: An edict ordered Cang each year to present to Yiwu cash of one hundred twenty thousand strings and grain of several tens of thousands of hu, with Yu as administrative aide.

units.zh: 武俊欲得滄，遣人說日華歸己，日華紿曰：「敝邑為賊攻，力屈則下之。
units.en: Wujun wanted Cang and sent envoys; Rihua deceived him, saying, "We are under attack—when we can no longer hold out we will submit to you.
units.literal: Wujun wished to obtain Cang and sent men to persuade Rihua to join him; Rihua deceived him, saying: "Our poor district is attacked by bandits; when our strength fails we shall submit.

units.zh: 願假騎二百以抗賊，賊退，請以地授公。」
units.en: Lend me two hundred horsemen to fight them off, and when the enemy retreats I will hand the land over to you."
units.literal: I wish to borrow two hundred cavalry to resist the bandits; when the bandits retreat, I ask to grant the territory to my lord."

units.zh: 武俊喜，歸之馬，日華留馬謝其使。
units.en: Wujun gladly sent the horses; Rihua kept them and thanked the envoy.
units.literal: Wujun was pleased and returned the horses; Rihua kept the horses and thanked his envoy.

units.zh: 武俊大怒，與滔方睦，懼有怨，乃止。
units.en: Wujun was furious, but he was allied with Zhu Tao and feared making another enemy, so he let the matter drop.
units.literal: Wujun was greatly enraged; he was then on friendly terms with Tao and feared creating enmity, and therefore desisted.

units.zh: 久之，武俊歸命，日華乃還馬，以珍幣厚謝，復結好，武俊亦釋然。
units.en: When Wujun eventually submitted to the court, Rihua returned the horses with lavish gifts, friendship was restored, and Wujun's anger faded.
units.literal: After a long time Wujun submitted to orders; Rihua then returned the horses, richly thanked him with precious goods, and renewed friendship; Wujun also felt relieved.

units.zh: 貞元二年卒，贈兵部尚書。
units.en: He died in Zhenyuan 2 (786) and was posthumously honored as Minister of War.
units.literal: He died in the second year of Zhenyuan and was posthumously granted Minister of War.

units.zh: 子懷直擅知留事，帝以日華故，即拜權知滄州刺史。
units.en: His son Huaizhi had taken charge in his absence; honoring Rihua's memory, the emperor named him acting prefect of Cang.
units.literal: His son Huaizhi on his own authority managed the acting governorship; because of Rihua the emperor at once appointed him acting prefect of Cang.

units.zh: 宇入朝，願析東光、景城二縣置景州，且請刺史。
units.en: Yu came to court and asked to carve Dongguang and Jingcheng into a new Jing Prefecture, with himself as prefect.
units.literal: Yu entered court and wished to split off the two counties Dongguang and Jingcheng to establish Jing Prefecture, and also requested to be its prefect.

units.zh: 河朔刺史不廷授幾三十年，帝嘉其忠，以徐申為景州刺史。
units.en: For nearly thirty years the court had not named a Hebei prefect directly; the emperor, admiring his loyalty, appointed Xu Shen to Jingzhou.
units.literal: Prefects of the Hebei-Shandong region had not been appointed by the court for nearly thirty years; the emperor praised his loyalty and appointed Xu Shen prefect of Jing.

units.zh: 升橫海軍為節度，擢懷直為留後。
units.en: Heng-Hai was raised to full circuit status and Huaizhi was made acting military governor.
units.literal: The Heng-Hai army was elevated to a circuit; Huaizhi was promoted to acting governor.

units.zh: 明年，為節度使。
units.en: The next year he was confirmed as military governor.
units.literal: The following year he became military governor.

units.zh: 九年來朝，寵遇加等，進檢校尚書右僕射，賜大第、宮女。
units.en: In his ninth year he visited court and was showered with honors—acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, a grand mansion, and palace women.
units.literal: In the ninth year he came to court; favor and treatment were doubled; he was advanced to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted a great mansion and palace women.

units.zh: 懷直荒田獵，出輒數日不返，帳下程懷信乘眾怒，閉門不納。
units.en: Huaizhi neglected his duties for hunting trips that lasted days; his officer Cheng Huaixin exploited the troops' anger and barred the gates against him.
units.literal: Huaizhi neglected government for hunting in the fields; when he went out he would not return for several days; his subordinate Cheng Huaixin seized on the troops' anger and shut the gates, refusing him entry.

units.zh: 懷信，其從昆也。
units.en: Huaixin was his cousin.
units.literal: Huaixin was his paternal cousin.

units.zh: 於是懷直入朝，帝不之罪，更以虔王為節度使，擢懷信留後，以懷直兼右龍武軍統軍。
units.en: Huaizhi went to court unpunished; the Prince of Qian was named military governor, Huaixin made acting governor, and Huaizhi was given a post in the Right Dragon Martial Guard.
units.literal: Thereupon Huaizhi entered court; the emperor did not punish him, instead replaced him with the Prince of Qian as military governor, promoted Huaixin to acting governor, and made Huaizhi concurrent commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.

units.zh: 明年，懷信為節度矣。
units.en: The next year Huaixin was confirmed as military governor.
units.literal: The following year Huaixin became military governor.

units.zh: 十六年，懷直卒，贈揚州大都督。
units.en: In the sixteenth year Huaizhi died and was posthumously honored as Grand Governor-General of Yangzhou.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year Huaizhi died and was posthumously granted Grand Protector General of Yang Prefecture.

units.zh: 後五年，懷信死，子權襲領軍務，詔授留後。
units.en: Five years later Huaixin died; his son Quan assumed command and was issued an edict acting governor.
units.literal: Five years later Huaixin died; his son Quan took over military affairs and was issued an edict as acting governor.

units.zh: 元和元年，拜節度使，累進檢校兵部尚書，封邢國公。
units.en: In Yuanhe 1 (806) he was confirmed military governor, rose to acting Minister of War, and was enfeoffed Duke of Xing.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe he was appointed military governor, repeatedly advanced to acting Minister of War, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.

units.zh: 六年入朝，憲宗寵禮遣還鎮，加檢校尚書右僕射。
units.en: In his sixth year he visited court; Xianzong honored him lavishly and sent him back with the title acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: In the sixth year he entered court; Xianzong favored and honored him and sent him back to his command, adding acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 權始名執恭，嘗夢滄諸門悉署「權」字，乃改名以應之。
units.en: Quan had been named Zhigong; he dreamed every gate in Cang bore the character "Quan" and changed his name accordingly.
units.literal: Quan was originally named Zhigong; he once dreamed that all the gates of Cang were inscribed with the character Quan, and therefore changed his name to correspond.

units.zh: 及淮西平，惕不安，丐入朝。
units.en: After the Huaixi campaign ended he grew uneasy and petitioned to come to court.
units.literal: When Huaixi was pacified he was fearful and uneasy and begged to enter court.

units.zh: 至京師，固辭軍政，乃詔華州刺史鄭權代之。
units.en: At the capital he firmly resigned his command; the court named Zheng Quan of Huazhou to replace him.
units.literal: When he reached the capital he firmly declined military administration; an edict then named the Huazhou prefect Zheng Quan to replace him.

units.zh: 後以檢校司空為邠寧節度使。
units.en: He later served as acting Minister of Works and military governor of Binning.
units.literal: Later, as acting Minister of Works, he became military governor of Binning.

units.zh: 卒，贈司徒，宗族奉朝請宿衛者三十餘人。
units.en: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor; more than thirty kinsmen held court gentleman posts in the palace guard.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Mentor; more than thirty of his clan served as court gentlemen in palace guard attendance.

units.zh: 李全略，李王氏，名日簡，事王武俊為偏裨。
units.en: Li Quanlüe, of the Li-Wang clan, named Rijian, had served Wang Wujun as a junior officer.
units.literal: Li Quanlüe was of the Li-Wang clan; his name was Rijian; he served Wang Wujun as a junior officer.

units.zh: 承宗時，虐用其軍，故入朝，授代州刺史。
units.en: Under Wang Chengzong he had abused his troops and fled to court, receiving appointment as prefect of Daizhou.
units.literal: Under Chengzong he cruelly exploited his army; therefore he entered court and was appointed prefect of Dai.

units.zh: 田弘正遇害，穆宗以全略故鎮州將，召問所欲言，全略多陳利害，冀合帝意，且請盡死力以報，遂授德州刺史。
units.en: After Tian Hongzheng's murder, Muzong summoned the former Zhenzhou officer Quanlüe for his views; Quanlüe laid out the strategic pros and cons, pledged his utmost loyalty, and was named prefect of Dezhou.
units.literal: When Tian Hongzheng was murdered, Muzong, because Quanlüe was a former Zhenzhou general, summoned him to ask what he wished to say; Quanlüe set forth many advantages and harms, hoping to accord with the emperor's mind, and also asked to exert his utmost strength in requital; he was thereupon appointed prefect of De.

units.zh: 是時，杜叔良兵敗博野，故以全略為橫海軍節度、滄德棣州觀察使，賜今姓名。
units.en: Du Shuliang had just been defeated at Boye; Quanlüe was made Heng-Hai military governor and surveillance commissioner over Cang, De, and Di, and granted the name Quanlüe.
units.literal: At that time Du Shuliang's army was defeated at Boye; therefore Quanlüe was made military governor of Heng-Hai and surveillance commissioner of Cang, De, and Di prefectures, and granted his present name.

units.zh: 未幾，貢錢千萬，使子同捷入朝。
units.en: Soon he sent ten million in cash as tribute and dispatched his son Tongjie to court.
units.literal: Before long he presented tribute of ten million in cash and sent his son Tongjie to court.

units.zh: 既還，即奏同捷為滄州長史，押中軍兵馬。
units.en: On returning he memorialized to name Tongjie chief administrator of Cangzhou and commander of the central army.
units.literal: When he returned he at once memorialized to make Tongjie chief administrator of Cang and controller of the central army's troops and horses.

units.zh: 帝不得已，可其請。
units.en: The emperor reluctantly consented.
units.literal: The emperor had no choice and approved his request.

units.zh: 全略陰規傳久計，選材武，以所私結士心。
units.en: Quanlüe secretly laid plans for his son to inherit power, picked able warriors, and won the officers' loyalty through personal favorites.
units.literal: Quanlüe secretly plotted a long-term plan of transmission, selected men of talent and martial skill, and with his favorites bound the hearts of the officers.

units.zh: 棣州刺史王稷善撫眾，而家富於財，全略內忌，以計殺之，族其家。
units.en: Di Prefecture's Wang Ji was beloved by his people and enormously wealthy; Quanlüe envied him, contrived his murder, and wiped out his entire family.
units.literal: The Di prefect Wang Ji was skilled at comforting the masses, yet his household was rich in wealth; Quanlüe inwardly envied him, killed him by stratagem, and exterminated his clan.

units.zh: 未幾死，同捷領留後事，重賂鄰藩，求領父節，敬宗持久詔不下。
units.en: He died soon after; Tongjie took over as acting governor, bribed neighboring circuits heavily, and petitioned to inherit his father's post—but Jingzong withheld confirmation for a long time.
units.literal: Before long he died; Tongjie took charge of acting governorship affairs, heavily bribed neighboring circuits, and sought to inherit his father's command; Jingzong long delayed the edict and did not issue it.

units.zh: 俄而文宗立，同捷以帝新嗣位，必大開貸示四方，乃遣弟同志、同巽入朝，而使其屬崔長奉表請命，有詔拜兗海節度使，以烏重胤代之。
units.en: When Wenzong succeeded, Tongjie assumed a new emperor would show leniency; he sent his brothers Tongzhi and Tongxun to court and had Cui Chang petition for confirmation—but the edict named him Yan-Hai governor and sent Wu Chongyin to replace him.
units.literal: Soon Wenzong ascended; Tongjie, thinking the emperor newly succeeded and would surely open wide favor to show the four quarters, sent his younger brothers Tongzhi and Tongxun to court and had his subordinate Cui Chang present a memorial requesting orders; an edict appointed him military governor of Yan-Hai and replaced him with Wu Chongyin.

units.zh: 同捷計窮，矯言軍中留己。
units.en: Cornered, Tongjie claimed the army would not let him leave.
units.literal: Tongjie's stratagems were exhausted; he falsely claimed the army detained him.

units.zh: 於是，王智興請以全軍出討，魏博史憲誠令大將傳手詔入於軍，同捷不受，德、棣民多奔入鄆。
units.en: Wang Zhixing offered his full army for the campaign; Shi Xiancheng of Weibo sent a general with the emperor's handwritten edict, which Tongjie refused; civilians from De and Di fled en masse into Yunzhou.
units.literal: Thereupon Wang Zhixing asked to lead his entire army out in punitive attack; Weibo's Shi Xiancheng ordered a great general to transmit the emperor's handwritten edict into the army; Tongjie would not accept it; the people of De and Di mostly fled into Yun.

units.zh: 乃下詔削官爵，命重胤率鄆、齊兵進討。
units.en: The court stripped his titles and ordered Wu Chongyin to lead Yun and Qi forces against him.
units.literal: An edict was then issued stripping his offices and titles and ordering Chongyin to lead Yan and Qi troops in advance attack.

units.zh: 憲誠、智興及汴滑李聽、平盧康志睦、易定張璠、幽州李載義以兵傅境。
units.en: Xiancheng, Zhixing, Li Ting of Bian-Hua, Kang Zhimu of Pinglu, Zhang Fan of Yiding, and Li Zaiyi of Youzhou all massed troops on his borders.
units.literal: Xiancheng, Zhixing, and Bian-Hua's Li Ting, Pinglu's Kang Zhimu, Yiding's Zhang Fan, and Youzhou's Li Zaiyi brought troops to the borders.

units.zh: 同捷自以與成德有舊，乃傾玉帛子女市河北三鎮。
units.en: Counting on old ties with Chengde, Tongjie lavished gold, silk, and daughters on the three northern circuits.
units.literal: Tongjie, considering himself to have old ties with Chengde, then poured out jade, silks, and daughters to buy the three Hebei circuits.

units.zh: 載義不許，絕其交，執使者並所遣奴婢四十七獻諸朝。
units.en: Li Zaiyi refused, cut ties, seized Tongjie's envoys and the forty-seven attendants they had brought, and sent them all to the capital.
units.literal: Zaiyi would not agree, broke off relations, seized the envoys together with the forty-seven slave women they had sent, and presented them to the court.

units.zh: 王廷湊本窺橫海，欲乘其隙取之，引軍來援。
units.en: Wang Tingcou had long eyed Heng-Hai and marched to Tongjie's aid, hoping to seize the circuit in the chaos.
units.literal: Wang Tingcou had long coveted Heng-Hai and wished to seize it by exploiting the opening; he led troops to come to Tongjie's aid.

units.zh: 智興攻棣州，火譙門，引水灌城，凡七月，其將張叔連降。
units.en: Zhixing besieged Di Prefecture for seven months, burned the gate tower, flooded the city, until his general Zhang Shulian surrendered.
units.literal: Zhixing attacked Di Prefecture, fired the watchtower gate, led water to flood the city—for seven months in all—until his general Zhang Shulian surrendered.

units.zh: 始，刺史欒濛以同捷叛，密上變，事泄，為所害，贈工部尚書。
units.en: Di's prefect Luan Meng had secretly reported Tongjie's rebellion; the plot leaked and Tongjie had him killed; he was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
units.literal: Earlier, the prefect Luan Meng, because Tongjie rebelled, secretly reported the emergency; the affair leaked and he was killed by them; posthumously he was granted Minister of Works.

units.zh: 智興進圍滄州。
units.en: Zhixing then besieged Cangzhou.
units.literal: Zhixing advanced to besiege Cang Prefecture.

units.zh: 是時，帝絕王廷湊朝貢，且討之，兵須夥繁，調發不時，始置供軍糧料使，以濟兩河，諸將又多張俘首以冒賞。
units.en: The emperor had cut off Wang Tingcou's tribute and was campaigning against him as well; troops were needed everywhere, supplies arrived late, and the court created the post of army-provisions commissioner for the two Hebei circuits—while generals inflated head counts to claim rewards.
units.literal: At that time the emperor cut off Wang Tingcou's court tribute and also attacked him; troops were needed in great numbers, levies were not timely, and for the first time the post of commissioner for army provisions and grain was established to aid the two Hebei circuits; the generals also often inflated captive heads to claim rewards.

units.zh: 自重胤卒後，李寰、傳良弼不終事，更以左金吾衛大將軍李祐代，而智興將李君謀以輕兵絕河，夜殘無棣，降饒安壁五千兵。
units.en: After Wu Chongyin died, Li Huan and Fu Liangbi failed to finish the job; Li You of the Left Golden Crow Guard replaced them; Zhixing's Li Junmou crossed the river with light troops, raided Wudi by night, and induced five thousand men at Raoyan to surrender.
units.literal: After Chongyin died, Li Huan and Fu Liangbi did not finish the task; Li You, great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, was substituted; Zhixing's general Li Junmou with light troops crossed the river, by night ravaged Wudi, and induced five thousand troops of the Raoyan rampart to surrender.

units.zh: 明年，祐拔無棣、平原。
units.en: The next year Li You captured Wudi and Pingyuan.
units.literal: The following year You took Wudi and Pingyuan.

units.zh: 有詔行營堅壁務農，非被襲，勿決戰。
units.en: An edict ordered the campaign armies to hold their walls and farm the land—no decisive battle unless attacked.
units.literal: An edict ordered the field headquarters to hold walls firm and devote themselves to agriculture; unless attacked, do not give decisive battle.

units.zh: 而祐兵已薄德州，帝遣諫議大夫柏耆宣慰。
units.en: Li You's army was already at Dezhou when the emperor sent Remonstrating Censor Bai Qi to offer terms.
units.literal: Meanwhile You's troops had already pressed close to De Prefecture; the emperor sent the Remonstrating Censor Bai Qi to proclaim consolation.

units.zh: 祐攻拔德州，餘卒奔廷湊。
units.en: You captured Dezhou; the survivors fled to Wang Tingcou.
units.literal: You attacked and took De Prefecture; the remaining troops fled to Tingcou.

units.zh: 同捷益急，乞降，祐疑其詐。
units.en: Tongjie, cornered, sued for surrender; Li You suspected a ruse.
units.literal: Tongjie grew ever more desperate and begged to surrender; You suspected deception.

units.zh: 耆引兵直入城，取同捷及家屬馳西。
units.en: Bai Qi marched straight into the city, seized Tongjie and his family, and raced west with them.
units.literal: Qi led troops straight into the city, seized Tongjie and his family, and galloped west.

units.zh: 祐入滄州，耆至將陵，斬同捷，使其下傳首京師。
units.en: You entered Cangzhou; at Jiangling, Bai Qi beheaded Tongjie and sent his head to Chang'an.
units.literal: You entered Cang Prefecture; when Qi reached Jiangling he beheaded Tongjie and had his subordinates send the head to the capital.

units.zh: 詔貸四州一年租賦，赦同捷母並妻息，徙湖南。
units.en: The court remitted a year's taxes for the four prefectures, pardoned Tongjie's mother, wife, and children, and exiled them to Hunan.
units.literal: An edict remitted one year's taxes and levies for the four prefectures, pardoned Tongjie's mother together with his wife and children, and exiled them to Hunan.

units.zh: 流崔長商州。
units.en: Cui Chang was banished to Shangzhou.
units.literal: Cui Chang was exiled to Shang Prefecture.

units.zh: 同巽等以異母貸死，得隨母流所云。
units.en: Tongxun and his half-brothers, as children of a concubine, were spared execution and allowed to accompany their mother into exile.
units.literal: Tongxun and the others, because they were born of a different mother, were spared death by a grant of clemency and were allowed to follow their mother to the place of exile, it is said.

units.zh: 及武元衡為宰相，以坦為中丞，李元素為大夫，命坦分司東都，未幾歸臺。
units.en: When Wu Yuanheng became chancellor, Tan was made vice censor-in-chief under chief censor Li Yuansu. Tan was posted separately to the eastern capital and soon returned to the Censorate.
units.literal: When Wu Yuanheng became chancellor, Tan was made vice censor-in-chief and Li Yuansu chief censor; Tan was ordered to serve separately at the eastern capital, and before long returned to the Censorate.

units.zh: 十一年九月，橫海大將程懷信逐其帥懷直。
units.en: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, Cheng Huaixin, a great general of Henghai, drove out his commander Huaizhi.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, the Henghai great general Cheng Huaixin drove out his commander Huaizhi.

units.zh: 王智興，字匡諫，懷州溫縣人也。
units.en: Wang Zhixing, styled Kuangjian, was a native of Wen County in Huai Prefecture.
units.literal: Wang Zhixing, style name Kuangjian, was a native of Wen County in Huai Prefecture.

units.zh: 自是，智興常以徐軍抗納，累歷滕、豐、沛、狄四鎮將。
units.en: Thereafter Zhixing led Xu troops against Na and in turn commanded the garrisons at Teng, Feng, Pei, and Di.
units.literal: From this, Zhixing constantly used the Xu army to resist Na, and successively served as garrison commander of the four posts Teng, Feng, Pei, and Di.

units.zh: 穆宗素知智興善將，遷檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，充武寧軍節度副使、河北行營都知兵馬使。
units.en: Muzong, knowing Zhixing's skill as a commander, promoted him to acting left regular attendant and censor grandee, made him vice military governor of the Wuning Army, and named him chief controller of the Hebei field headquarters.
units.literal: Muzong had long known Zhixing was skilled as a general; he was transferred to Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently Censor Grandee, serving as Vice Military Governor of the Wuning Army and Chief Controller of Military Affairs for the Hebei Field Headquarters.

units.zh: 智興少驍銳，為徐州衙卒，事刺史李洧。
units.en: In youth Zhixing was bold and keen; he served as a Xu Prefecture yamen soldier under Prefect Li Wei.
units.literal: Zhixing in youth was fierce and sharp; he was a Xu Prefecture yamen soldier and served Prefect Li Wei.

units.zh: 累官至侍御史、本軍都押衙。
units.en: He rose to palace censor and chief superintendent of the circuit army.
units.literal: He cumulatively reached the office of Palace Censor and Chief Superintendent of the Circuit Army.

units.zh: 德宗發朔方軍五千人隨智興赴之，淄青圍解。
units.en: Dezong sent five thousand Shuo-fang troops with Zhixing to the rescue, and the Ziqing siege was broken.
units.literal: Dezong dispatched five thousand Shuo-fang troops to follow Zhixing and go to their aid; the Zi-qing siege was lifted.

units.zh: 元和中，王師誅吳元濟，李師道與蔡賊謀撓沮王師，頻出軍侵徐，徐帥李願以所部步騎悉委智興以抗之。
units.en: During the Yuanhe reign, while imperial forces campaigned to destroy Wu Yuanji, Li Shidao joined the Cai rebels in harassing the court's armies and repeatedly raided Xu; Military Governor Li Yuan put all his infantry and cavalry under Zhixing to repel them.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe reign, the imperial army executed Wu Yuanji; Li Shidao with the Cai rebels plotted to thwart and discourage the imperial army, frequently sending out troops to invade Xu; the Xu commander Li Yuan entrusted all the infantry and cavalry under his command to Zhixing to resist them.

units.zh: 十三年，王師誅李師道，智興率徐軍八千會諸道之師進擊。
units.en: In the thirteenth year (818), as the imperial army moved to destroy Li Shidao, Zhixing led eight thousand Xu troops to join the allied armies in the advance.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year, the imperial army executed Li Shidao; Zhixing led eight thousand Xu troops to join the armies of the various circuits in advancing to attack.

units.zh: 長慶初，河朔復亂，征兵進討。
units.en: Early in the Changqing reign, Hebei erupted in rebellion again, and the court mobilized troops for a punitive campaign.
units.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, Hebei again fell into disorder; troops were levied to advance and punish.

units.zh: 父縉，太子詹事。
units.en: His father Jin served as Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: His father Jin was Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 祖瑰，右金吾衛將軍。
units.en: His grandfather Gui was general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
units.literal: His grandfather Gui was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

units.zh: 曾祖靖，左武衛將軍。
units.en: His great-grandfather Jing served as general of the Left Martial Guard.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Jing was General of the Left Martial Guard.

units.zh: 智興健行，不四五日賫表京師求援。
units.en: Zhixing was a strong runner; within four or five days he carried memorials swiftly to the capital seeking relief.
units.literal: Zhixing was a strong traveler; in no more than four or five days he carried memorials swiftly to the capital to seek relief.

units.zh: 自是二十余年為徐將。
units.en: For more than twenty years thereafter he served as a Xu commander.
units.literal: From this for more than twenty years he was a Xu commander.

units.zh: 鄆將王朝晏以兵攻沛，智興擊敗之。
units.en: Yan commander Wang Chaoyan attacked Pei; Zhixing routed him.
units.literal: The Yan commander Wang Chaoyan attacked Pei with troops; Zhixing struck and defeated him.

units.zh: 賊又令姚海率勁兵二萬圍豐，攻城甚急。
units.en: The rebels next sent Yao Hai with twenty thousand elite troops to besiege Feng in a fierce assault.
units.literal: The rebels again ordered Yao Hai to lead twenty thousand crack troops to besiege Feng; the assault on the city was very urgent.

units.zh: 智興復擊敗之。
units.en: Zhixing defeated them again.
units.literal: Zhixing again struck and defeated them.

units.zh: 於賊壁獲美妾，智興懼軍士爭之，乃曰：「軍中有女子，安得不敗？
units.en: After capturing a beautiful woman in the enemy camp, Zhixing feared the troops would fight over her and said, "An army that keeps women cannot help but be defeated.
units.literal: At the rebel ramparts he captured a beautiful concubine; Zhixing feared the soldiers would quarrel over her, and therefore said: "When there are women in the army, how can one not be defeated?

units.zh: 此雖無罪，違軍法也。」
units.en: Though she is innocent, this violates military law."
units.literal: Although this person is without guilt, it violates military law."

units.zh: 即斬之以徇。
units.en: He beheaded her on the spot as an example.
units.literal: He immediately beheaded her to display.

units.zh: 與陳許之軍大破賊於金鄉，拔魚臺，俘斬萬計，以功遷御史中丞。
units.en: With the Chenxu army he routed the rebels at Jinxiang, took Yutai, and killed or captured tens of thousands; for this he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: With the Chen and Xu armies he greatly defeated the rebels at Jinxiang, captured Yutai, and captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands; for merit he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 賊平，授沂州刺史。
units.en: After the rebellion was suppressed, he was appointed prefect of Yi Prefecture.
units.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Prefect of Yi Prefecture.

units.zh: 洧遂以徐州歸國。
units.en: Wei thereupon submitted Xu Prefecture to the Tang court.
units.literal: Wei then submitted Xu Prefecture to the state.

units.zh: 李希烈揣知之，上表數崇義過惡，請率先誅討。
units.en: Li Xilie divined their intent and submitted a memorial listing Chongyi's crimes, asking to take the lead in punishing him.
units.literal: Li Xilie guessed their intent and submitted a memorial listing Chongyi's faults, asking to take the lead in punishment.

units.zh: 無幾，希烈既平崇義，果有不順之跡，上思承言，故驟加擢用。
units.en: Before long Xilie had pacified Chongyi and indeed showed signs of rebellion; the emperor recalled Cheng's warning and swiftly promoted him.
units.literal: Before long Xilie had pacified Chongyi and indeed showed signs of disobedience; the emperor recalled Cheng's words and swiftly promoted him.

units.zh: 建中二年七月，拜同州刺史、河中尹、晉絳都防禦觀察使。
units.en: In the seventh month of 781 he was made prefect of Tong, mayor of the Hezhong metropolitan area, and commissioner of defense and observation for Jin and Jiang.
units.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianzhong he was made Prefect of Tong, Mayor of the Hezhong metropolitan area, and Commissioner of Defense and Observation for Jin and Jiang.

units.zh: 希烈既破崇義，擁兵襄州，遂有其地。
units.en: After Xilie defeated Chongyi he massed troops at Xiangzhou and thereupon held that territory.
units.literal: After Xilie had defeated Chongyi he massed troops at Xiangzhou and thereupon held that territory.

units.zh: 希烈不能屈，遂剽虜闔境所有而去，襄、漢為之空。
units.en: Xilie could not break him; he then plundered everything of value in the circuit and withdrew, leaving Xiang and Han stripped bare.
units.literal: Xilie could not break him; he then plundered all goods in the circuit and departed, and Xiang and Han were left empty.

units.zh: 上悅之，每對朝臣多稱希烈忠誠。
units.en: The emperor was pleased; before the court he often praised Xilie's loyalty.
units.literal: The emperor was pleased; facing court ministers he often praised Xilie's loyalty.

units.zh: 承自黜陟回，因奏之曰：「希烈將兵討伐，必有微勛，但恐立功之後，縱恣跋扈，不稟朝憲，必勞王師問罪。」
units.en: When Cheng returned from his commission, he memorialized: "Xilie will surely win some merit on campaign—but I fear that once he has merit he will grow insolent and defiant, disregard imperial authority, and the royal army will be forced to march against him."
units.literal: When Cheng returned from his commission, he memorialized: "Xilie will surely win some merit campaigning—but I fear that after merit he will grow insolent and defiant, disobey imperial law, and the royal army will labor to punish him."

units.zh: 朝廷慮不受命，欲以禁兵送承，承請單騎徑行。
units.en: The court feared Xilie would refuse the appointment and wished to send palace troops to escort Cheng; Cheng asked to ride through alone.
units.literal: The court feared he would not accept orders and wished to send palace troops to escort Cheng; Cheng asked to ride alone straight through.

units.zh: 既至，希烈處承於外館，迫脅萬態，承恬然自安，誓死王事。
units.en: When he arrived, Xilie lodged Cheng in an outer guesthouse and assailed him with every sort of coercion; Cheng remained calm, sworn to the throne unto death.
units.literal: When he arrived, Xilie lodged Cheng in an outer guesthouse and coerced him with every manner of threat; Cheng remained calm and at ease, sworn to royal service unto death.

units.zh: 初，希烈雖歸蔡州，留將校等於襄州守當時所掠得財帛什物等，後使襄、漢，往來不絕。
units.en: At first, though Xilie had returned to Cai prefecture, he left officers at Xiang to guard the goods plundered there; afterward traffic between Xiang and Han never ceased.
units.literal: At first, though Xilie had returned to Cai prefecture, he left officers and clerks at Xiang to guard the property and goods looted at the time; afterward envoys between Xiang and Han never ceased.

units.zh: 承亦使腹心臧叔雅往來許、蔡，厚結希烈腹心周曾、王玢、姚憺等。
units.en: Cheng also sent his trusted agent Zang Shuya back and forth between Xu and Cai, lavishly cultivating Xilie's intimates Zhou Ceng, Wang Bin, Yao Tan, and others.
units.literal: Cheng also sent his trusted follower Zang Shuya back and forth between Xu and Cai, richly cultivating Xilie's intimates Zhou Ceng, Wang Bin, Yao Tan, and others.

units.zh: 及曾等謀殺希烈，以眾歸朝，多承首建謀也。
units.en: When Ceng and the others plotted to kill Xilie and bring their forces back to the court, the plan owed much to Cheng's original design.
units.literal: When Ceng and the rest plotted to kill Xilie and bring the hosts back to the court, the plan owed much to Cheng's first design.

units.zh: 列傳第一百三十一史憲誠史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今爲靈武建康人。
units.en: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. His ancestors originally sprang from the Xi people; in his day Shi Xiancheng was reckoned a man of Jiankang in Lingwu.
units.literal: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. Shi Xiancheng — his ancestors came from the Xi barbarians; he is now registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.

units.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。
units.en: Xiancheng first made his name through ability and valor, serving beside his father in senior army posts while also holding the post of Investigating Censor.
units.literal: Xiancheng began by virtue of talent and courage; following his father he held senior posts in the army and concurrently served as Investigating Censor.

units.zh: 旋聞絺爲帳下所殺，乃從改過，謂文恪曰：「憲誠蕃人，猶狗也，唯能識主。
units.en: When he soon heard that Qi had been killed by his own officers, he changed his tune and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian—no better than a dog—and knows only his master.
