units.literal: Soon hearing that Qi had been killed by his subordinates, he then changed his ways and said to Wenke: "Xiancheng is a barbarian, like a dog — he can only recognize his master.

units.zh: 太和三年，軍眾害史憲誠，連聲而呼曰：「得衙內都知兵馬使何端公知留後，即三軍安矣。」
units.en: In the third year of Taihe the soldiers killed Shi Xiancheng and cried out together, "Let Lord He, the chief controller of the headquarters guard, take charge as acting governor, and the three armies will be settled."
units.literal: In the third year of Taihe the troops killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted in unison: "If the Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry within the headquarters guard, Lord He of Duan, becomes acting military governor, the three armies will be at peace."

units.zh: 變易主帥，有同兒戲，如史憲誠、何進滔、韓君雄、樂彥禎，皆爲其所立。
units.en: They changed commanders as casually as children at play; Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen had all been set up by them.
units.literal: They changed commanders as easily as child's play; Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all installed by them.

units.zh: 憲誠爲中軍都知兵馬使，乘亂以河朔舊事動其人心，諸軍即擁而歸魏，共立爲帥，國家因而命之。
units.en: Xiancheng, as chief controller of the central army's horse and foot, used the disorder to appeal to the old ways of the Hebei garrisons; the troops at once rallied back to Wei, set him up as their leader, and the throne confirmed the appointment.
units.literal: Xiancheng was Chief Controller of Cavalry and Infantry of the central army; exploiting the chaos he stirred the troops' hearts with old customs of the Hebei region, the armies immediately rallied and returned to Wei, jointly installing him as commander, and the state accordingly appointed him.

units.zh: 時克融、廷湊並據兵爲亂，憲誠喜得旄節，雖外順朝旨，而中與硃、王爲輔車之勢，長慶二年正月也。
units.en: Kerong and Tingcou were both in arms against the court; Xiancheng was delighted to receive the commander's baton and banner. Outwardly he followed the court's orders, yet inwardly he and Zhu and Wang lent each other the support of linked chariots — all this in the first month of the second year of Changqing.
units.literal: At the time Kerong and Tingcou both held troops in rebellion; Xiancheng rejoiced at receiving the commander's baton and banner. Though outwardly he obeyed the court's intent, inwardly he stood in mutual support with Zhu and Wang — this was in the first month of the second year of Changqing.

units.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。
units.en: During the Yuanhe reign, when Tian Hongzheng marched against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng ahead with four thousand vanguard troops to cross the Yellow River and take one fortified camp after another.
units.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to cross the river with four thousand vanguard troops, repeatedly capturing his fortified camps.

units.zh: 憲誠心不自安，乃遣子孝章入覲，又飛章願以所管奉命。
units.en: Uneasy in his own mind, Xiancheng sent his son Xiaozhang to court and dispatched urgent memorials offering to place his command under the throne's orders.
units.literal: Xiancheng felt ill at ease in his heart; he then sent his son Xiaozhang to court for audience, and also sent urgent memorials offering to place his jurisdiction under court command.

units.zh: 憲誠子 孝章孝章，幼聰悟好學。
units.en: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang was clever from childhood and devoted to study.
units.literal: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang — from youth he was clever and fond of learning.

units.zh: 太和二年，滄景節度使李全略卒，其子同捷竊據軍城，表邀符節，舉兵伐之。
units.en: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the garrison city and memorialized for the commander's seal and baton, whereupon the court mobilized an army against him.
units.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the military city by stealth, memorialized requesting the seal and baton of command, and the court raised troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 未及出城，太和三年六月二十六日夜，爲軍眾所害，冊贈太尉。
units.en: Before he could even leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month in the third year of Taihe, his own soldiers killed him; the court posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Before he could leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of the third year of Taihe, he was killed by the troops; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。
units.en: When his merits were entered on the rolls, Xiancheng was promoted out of turn to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: His achievements were recorded, and Xiancheng was exceptionally promoted to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 朝廷每爲優容，尋加左僕射。
units.en: The court repeatedly indulged him, and soon promoted him to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: The court repeatedly showed him forbearance, and soon added the post of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 敬宗即位，進秩司空。
units.en: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, Xiancheng was advanced to Grand Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, he was promoted to Grand Minister of Works.

units.zh: 上屢發使申諭，尋又就加平章事。
units.en: The emperor sent envoys again and again to warn him, and soon added the title of Grand Councilor as well.
units.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to instruct and admonish him, and soon additionally appointed him Grand Councilor.

units.zh: 及滄景平，加司徒。
units.en: When Cangjing was pacified, he was made Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When Cangjing was pacified, he was promoted to Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 乃加侍中，移鎮河中。
units.en: He was made Palace Attendant and transferred to Hezhong.
units.literal: He was then made Palace Attendant and transferred to govern Hezhong.

units.zh: 先是，憲誠與全略婚媾，及同捷叛，復潛以糧餉爲助。
units.en: Xiancheng had earlier been linked to Quanlue by marriage; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly supplied him with grain and fodder.
units.literal: Earlier Xiancheng had been allied by marriage with Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly aided him with provisions.

units.zh: 其狡譎如此。
units.en: Such was the depth of his cunning.
units.literal: Such was his cunning and deceit.

units.zh: 雖被棒打，終不忍離。」
units.en: Beat him as you will with a stick, yet he cannot bear to leave his master's side."
units.literal: Even if beaten with a stick, he could never bear to leave."

units.zh: 時李㝏爲亂，與憲誠書問交通。
units.en: Li Qi was then in rebellion and kept up a correspondence with Xiancheng.
units.literal: At the time Li Qi was in rebellion and exchanged letters with Xiancheng.

units.zh: 憲誠表請與㝏節鉞，仍於黎陽艤舟，示欲渡河。
units.en: Xiancheng memorialized asking for the same command baton as Qi, and moored boats at Liyang as if preparing to cross the river.
units.literal: Xiancheng memorialized requesting the same military commission as Qi, and moreover anchored boats at Liyang to show intent to cross the river.

units.zh: 憲誠嘗遣驍將至闕下，恣爲張大，宰相韋處厚以語折剉之，憲誠不敢復與同捷爲應。
units.en: Xiancheng once sent bold generals to the capital who swaggered without restraint; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou put them down with sharp words, and Xiancheng no longer dared to act in concert with Tongjie.
units.literal: Xiancheng once sent fierce generals to the capital who acted with reckless arrogance; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuked them with words, and Xiancheng dared not again coordinate with Tongjie.

units.zh: 時憲誠示出師共討同捷。
units.en: For a time Xiancheng made a show of marching out to join the campaign against Tongjie.
units.literal: At the time Xiancheng made a show of setting out with troops to join in attacking Tongjie together.

units.zh: 憲誠素懷向背，不能以忠誠感激其眾。
units.en: Xiancheng had long wavered between loyalty and defiance and could not win his troops over with steadfast devotion.
units.literal: Xiancheng had long harbored divided loyalties and could not move his followers with sincerity and devotion.

units.zh: 及憲誠領節鉞，改士曹參軍、兼監察御史，賜緋。
units.en: When Xiancheng took the command baton, Xiaozhang was made Staff Officer of the Personnel Section and concurrent Investigating Censor, with scarlet robes bestowed on him.
units.literal: When Xiancheng received the military commission, Xiaozhang was changed to Staff Officer of the Personnel Section, concurrent Investigating Censor, and granted scarlet robes.

units.zh: 尋請赴闕，文宗慰勞甚厚，憲誠亦因懇乞朝覲。
units.en: He soon asked leave to come to court; Emperor Wenzong received him with generous praise, and Xiancheng too pressed his petition to attend in person.
units.literal: Soon he requested to go to court; Emperor Wenzong comforted and rewarded him generously, and Xiancheng also earnestly begged to attend court.

units.zh: 上知憲誠之入覲，自孝章之謀，遂加禮部尚書，分相、衞、澶三州別爲一鎮，俾孝章領之。
units.en: The emperor understood that Xiancheng's wish to attend court came from Xiaozhang's counsel; he therefore made Xiaozhang Minister of Rites, carved out Xiang, Wei, and Chan as a separate command, and put Xiaozhang in charge of it.
units.literal: The emperor knew that Xiancheng's coming to court sprang from Xiaozhang's plan; he then added the post of Minister of Rites, separated the three prefectures of Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate command, and had Xiaozhang govern it.

units.zh: 孝章未到鎮，憲誠遇害。
units.en: Before Xiaozhang could reach his new command, Xiancheng was killed.
units.literal: Before Xiaozhang reached his post, Xiancheng met a violent death.

units.zh: 鄭權因鄭註得廣州節度，權至鎮，盡以公家珍寶赴京師以酬恩地。
units.en: Zheng Quan obtained the Guangzhou commission through Zheng Zhu. When Quan reached his post, he sent all the state's precious treasures to the capital to repay his patron.
units.literal: Zheng Quan, through Zheng Zhu, obtained the Guangzhou military commission; when Quan reached his command, he sent all the state's precious treasures to the capital to repay the source of his favor.

units.zh: 廷老上疏請按權罪，中人由是切齒。
units.en: Tinglao submitted a memorial demanding an investigation of Quan's crimes. Inner attendants gnashed their teeth at him.
units.literal: Tinglao submitted a memorial requesting investigation of Quan's crimes; inner attendants thereby gnashed their teeth at him.

units.zh: 初，以柳公綽在鎮無功，議將代之，裴度言：「道古嗣曹王皋之子，皋嘗以江漢兵遏希烈之亂，威惠至今在人，復用其子必能繼美。」
units.en: When Liu Gongchuo's tenure had yielded no results, the court considered replacing him. Pei Du argued, "Li Daogu is the son of Prince of Cao Li Gao. Li Gao once held the Jiang-Han line against Li Xilie's rebellion, and his prestige and kindness are remembered to this day. Appointing his son would carry on that legacy."
units.literal: Initially, because Liu Gongchuo at his post had no achievements, there was discussion of replacing him; Pei Du said: "Daogu is heir as son of Prince of Cao Gao; Gao once with Jiang-Han troops checked Xi Lie's rebellion; prestige and kindness remain in people's hearts to this day; employing his son again will surely be able to continue the excellence."

units.zh: 時公綽殊未意道古至，惶駭而出，家財多為所奪。
units.en: Liu Gongchuo had no warning of his arrival and fled in panic. Li Daogu seized much of his household property.
units.literal: At that time Gongchuo had no idea Daogu would arrive; he fled in panic and alarm; much household property was seized by him.

units.zh: 馬燧前賀曰：今之一盟，百年內更無蕃寇。」
units.en: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying, "With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids."
units.literal: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying: 'With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids.'

units.zh: 次子延嗣竊立，尋為大將李載義所殺。
units.en: Kerong's second son Yansi seized power on his own authority, but was soon killed by the general Li Zaiyi.
units.literal: The second son Yansi seized power in his stead and was soon killed by the great general Li Zaiyi.

units.zh: 李載義，字方谷，常山湣王之後。
units.en: Li Zaiyi, styled Fanggu, was a descendant of the Prince Min of Changshan.
units.literal: Li Zaiyi, styled Fanggu, was a descendant of the Prince Min of Changshan.

units.zh: 敬宗嘉之，拜檢校戶部尚書、兼御史大夫，封武威郡王，充幽州盧龍等軍節度副大使，知節度事。
units.en: Emperor Jingzong praised his action and appointed him acting Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed him as Prince of Wuwei Commandery, and made him vice military governor of the Youzhou-Lulong circuit with full control of its affairs.
units.literal: Emperor Jingzong commended him, appointing him acting Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffing him as Prince of Wuwei Commandery, and making him vice military governor of the Youzhou-Lulong armies with charge of military governorship affairs.

units.zh: 開成二年卒，年五十，贈太尉。
units.en: In the second year of Kaicheng, he died at the age of fifty and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.
units.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng, he died at the age of fifty and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 劉濟為幽州節度使，見而偉之，致於親軍，從征伐。
units.en: When Liu Ji served as military governor of Youzhou, he was struck by Zaiyi's imposing bearing, enrolled him in his personal guard, and took him on campaign.
units.literal: When Liu Ji was military governor of Youzhou, he saw him and admired his stature, brought him into his personal guard, and took him on campaigns.

units.zh: 載義少孤，與鄉曲之不令者遊。
units.en: Zaiyi lost his father while still young and kept company with unruly men of the neighborhood.
units.literal: Zaiyi was orphaned young and consorted with disreputable locals.

units.zh: 丁母憂，起復驃騎大將軍，餘如故。
units.en: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning as General of Chariots and Cavalry while retaining his other posts.
units.literal: On mourning for his mother he was recalled from mourning as General of Chariots and Cavalry; the rest of his posts remained unchanged.

units.zh: 有勇力，善挽強角牴。
units.en: He was brave and powerful, and excelled at drawing heavy bows and wrestling.
units.literal: He had courage and strength and was skilled at drawing the heavy bow and wrestling.

units.zh: 以功遷衙前都知兵馬使，檢校光祿大夫、兼監察御史。
units.en: For his achievements he was promoted to commander of the vanguard guard, with the acting rank of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and the concurrent post of investigating censor.
units.literal: For merit he was promoted to commander of the vanguard guard, acting Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and concurrently investigating censor.

units.zh: 載義遂殺之，數其罪以聞。
units.en: Zaiyi then killed him, listed his crimes, and reported the matter to the court.
units.literal: Zaiyi then killed him and enumerated his crimes in a report.

units.zh: 載義上表，請討同捷以自效。
units.en: Zaiyi memorialized the throne, asking permission to campaign against Tongjie as proof of his loyalty.
units.literal: Zaiyi submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against Tongjie to prove his loyalty.

units.zh: 累破賊軍，以功加司空，進階金紫，
units.en: He repeatedly routed the rebel armies, and for his achievements was promoted to Minister of Works (Sikong) and advanced to the rank of Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia.
units.literal: He repeatedly defeated rebel armies; for merit he was made Minister of Works (Sikong) and advanced to the Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia rank.

units.zh: 上嘉其誠懇，特加檢校右僕射。
units.en: The emperor was pleased by his earnestness and specially added the acting post of Right Vice Director.
units.literal: The emperor commended his sincerity and specially added the post of acting Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 太和三年，平滄景，策勛加平章事，仍賜實封三百戶。
units.en: In the third year of Taihe, after pacifying Cangzhou and Jingzhou he was made Grand Counselor in recognition of his merit and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.
units.literal: In the third year of Taihe, he pacified Cang and Jing; for his recorded merit he was made Grand Counselor and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.

units.zh: 四年，契丹寇邊，以兵擊走之，仍虜其名王，就加太保。
units.en: In the fourth year, when the Khitan raided the frontier, he drove them off by force and captured one of their royal leaders; he was thereupon promoted to Grand Guardian.
units.literal: In the fourth year the Khitan raided the border; he drove them off with troops and captured one of their royal leaders, whereupon he was made Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 五年春，為其部下楊志誠所逐，因入覲。
units.en: In the spring of the fifth year his subordinate Yang Zhicheng drove him out, and he came to court to pay homage.
units.literal: In spring of the fifth year he was driven out by his subordinate Yang Zhicheng and therefore came to court for an audience.

units.zh: 上以載義有平滄景之功，又能恭順朝旨，再拜太保、同平章事。
units.en: Because Zaiyi had pacified Cangzhou and Jingzhou and had shown himself obedient to the court, the emperor again appointed him Grand Guardian and Concurrent Grand Counselor.
units.literal: The emperor, because Zaiyi had merit in pacifying Cang and Jing and could respectfully follow court directives, again appointed him Grand Guardian and Concurrent Grand Counselor.

units.zh: 其年，改山南西道節度、觀察等使，兼興元尹。
units.en: That same year he was transferred to military governor and surveillance commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, concurrently serving as governor of Xingyuan.
units.literal: That year he was transferred to be military governor and surveillance commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, concurrently governor of Xingyuan.

units.zh: 七年，遷北都留守，兼太原尹，充河東節度觀察處置等使。
units.en: In the seventh year he was transferred to defender of the Northern Capital, concurrently governor of Taiyuan and military governor, surveillance commissioner, and disposal commissioner of Hedong.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to be defender of the Northern Capital, concurrently governor of Taiyuan, serving as military governor, surveillance commissioner, and disposal commissioner of Hedong.

units.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司。
units.en: He was soon further honored with the prestige rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi (privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers).
units.literal: Soon he was additionally granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with the same honors as the Three Ducal Ministers.

units.zh: 載義因召李暢與語曰：「可汗使將軍朝貢，以固舅甥之好，不當使將軍暴踐中華。
units.en: Zaiyi summoned Li Chang and said to him, "The qaghan sent you to pay tribute and strengthen the bond between uncle and nephew. He did not send you to rampage through the Central Realm.
units.literal: Zaiyi therefore summoned Li Chang and spoke to him, saying: "The qaghan sent the general to pay court tribute in order to strengthen the bond of uncle and nephew; he should not have the general trample violently upon the Central Realm.

units.zh: 遂罷防守之兵，而使兩卒司其門。
units.en: He then dismissed the guard troops and posted only two soldiers at their gate.
units.literal: He then dismissed the guarding troops and had only two soldiers keep watch at the gate.

units.zh: 今朝廷饔餼至厚，所以禮蕃客也。
units.en: The court now provides you with lavish hospitality — that is how foreign guests are to be treated.
units.literal: Now the court's provisions are extremely generous — that is how foreign guests are treated.

units.zh: 茍有不至，吏當坐死。
units.en: If anything is lacking, the officials responsible deserve death.
units.literal: If anything falls short, the officials should be punished with death.

units.zh: 若將軍之部伍不戢，淩侮上國，剽掠廬舍，載義必殺為盜者。
units.en: But if your men cannot keep discipline, insult this realm, and plunder people's homes, I will kill anyone who behaves like a bandit.
units.literal: If the general's troops are not restrained, insult the superior state, and plunder dwellings, Zaiyi will surely kill those who act as bandits.

units.zh: 將軍勿以法令可輕而不戒勵之！」
units.en: General, do not imagine that the law may be treated lightly — warn your men and keep them in order!"
units.literal: General, do not think the laws can be treated lightly and fail to warn and restrain them!"

units.zh: 九年，加侍中。
units.en: In the ninth year he was appointed Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the ninth year he was made Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 載義晚年驕恣，慘暴一方。
units.en: In his later years Zaiyi grew arrogant and tyrannical, ruling his region with cruel violence.
units.literal: In his later years Zaiyi was arrogant and willful, cruel and violent over his region.

units.zh: 以楊志誠復為部下所逐，過太原，載義躬身毆擊，遂欲殺之，賴從事救解以免。
units.en: When Yang Zhicheng was again ousted by his own men and passed through Taiyuan, Zaiyi personally assaulted him and tried to kill him; only the intervention of a staff officer saved Zhicheng.
units.literal: When Yang Zhicheng was again driven out by his subordinates and passed through Taiyuan, Zaiyi personally beat him and then tried to kill him; he escaped only because a staff officer intervened to save him.

units.zh: 然而擅殺志誠之妻孥及將卒。
units.en: Even so, he arbitrarily executed Zhicheng's wife, children, and accompanying officers and soldiers.
units.literal: Nevertheless he killed Zhicheng's wife, children, and officers and soldiers on his own authority.

units.zh: 寶歷中，幽師殺硃克融。
units.en: During the Baoli era the Youzhou army killed Zhu Kerong.
units.literal: During the Baoli reign, the Youzhou army killed Zhu Kerong.

units.zh: 代以武力稱，繼為幽州屬郡守。
units.en: His family had long been known for martial prowess, and he inherited a post as prefect of a Youzhou subordinate commandery.
units.literal: His family for generations was famed for martial prowess; he succeeded to be prefect of a subordinate commandery in Youzhou.

units.zh: 楊志誠，太和五年為幽州後院副兵馬使，事李載義。
units.en: Yang Zhicheng was in the fifth year of Taihe made deputy commander of the Youzhou rear guard under Li Zaiyi.
units.literal: Yang Zhicheng — in the fifth year of Taihe he was deputy commander of the rear guard in Youzhou and served Li Zaiyi.

units.zh: 時朝廷賜載義德政碑文。
units.en: At that time the court had granted Zaiyi a stele commemorating his virtuous rule.
units.literal: At that time the court granted Zaiyi a stele inscription praising his virtuous administration.

units.zh: 載義延中使擊鞠，志誠亦與焉，遂於鞠場叫呼謀亂。
units.en: Zaiyi entertained the imperial envoy with a game of cuju, and Zhicheng joined in; at the playing field Zhicheng suddenly shouted and incited a mutiny.
units.literal: Zaiyi invited the imperial envoy to play cuju; Zhicheng also took part, and then at the cuju field shouted and plotted mutiny.

units.zh: 載義奔於易州，志誠乃為本道馬步都知兵馬使。
units.en: Zaiyi fled to Yizhou, and Zhicheng made himself overall commander of the circuit's cavalry and infantry.
units.literal: Zaiyi fled to Yizhou, and Zhicheng then became overall commander of cavalry and infantry in the circuit.

units.zh: 則今日志誠之得，猶前日載義之得也。
units.en: Zhicheng's rise today is no different from Zaiyi's rise yesterday.
units.literal: Then Zhicheng's gaining power today is just like Zaiyi's gaining power the other day.

units.zh: 張宿者，本寒人，自名諸生。
units.en: Zhang Su was born poor yet called himself a literatus.
units.literal: Zhang Su came from humble origins yet styled himself a scholar.

units.zh: 及監撫，自布衣授左拾遺，交通權幸，四方賂遺滿門。
units.en: On becoming heir apparent he rose from commoner to Left Reminder, courted favorites, and gifts from every quarter clogged his door.
units.literal: When appointed heir he was raised from common cloth to Left Reminder, trafficked with the powerful, and bribes from the four quarters filled his gate.

units.zh: 憲宗為廣陵王時，因張茂宗薦尉，得出入邸中，誕譎敢言。
units.en: As Prince of Guangling, Xianzong took him in through Zhang Maozong as aide; he entered the mansion, sly and outspoken.
units.literal: When Xianzong was Prince of Guangling, through Zhang Maozong's recommendation as aide he gained access to the prince's residence, crafty and bold in speech.

units.zh: 元和末，持節至淄青，李師道願割地遣子入侍。
units.en: Late in Yuanhe he bore credentials to Ziqing; Li Shidao offered to yield land and send his son to court.
units.literal: At the end of Yuanhe he held credentials to Ziqing; Li Shidao wished to cede territory and send his son to court as hostage.

units.zh: 數召對，不能慎密，坐漏禁中語，貶郴丞十餘年。
units.en: Called to audience repeatedly, he could not hold his tongue and was demoted to Chen aide for over ten years for leaking inner-court words.
units.literal: Summoned to audience many times, he could not keep secrets and was demoted to Chen prefecture aide for more than ten years for leaking palace speech.

units.zh: 既而悔，復遣宿往，暴卒於道，贈秘書監。
units.en: He then regretted it and sent Su again; Su died suddenly on the road and was posthumously made Secretariat Director.
units.literal: Then he repented and sent Su again; Su died violently on the road and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 宿怨執政不與己，乃日肆讒甚，與皇甫镈相附離，多中傷正人君子。
units.en: Su hated the chancellors for not backing him and daily slandered, clinging to Huangfu Bo and wounding upright men.
units.literal: Su resented the rulers for not siding with him and daily poured out slander, attaching himself to Huangfu Bo and striking at upright gentlemen.

units.zh: 宰相李逢吉數言其狡譎不可信，白為濠州刺史，宿上疏自言，留不遣。
units.en: Fengji often called him treacherous and had him sent to Hao as prefect; Su petitioned in his own defense and was kept at court.
units.literal: Chancellor Li Fengji often said he was cunning and untrustworthy and had him made prefect of Hao; Su memorialized on his own behalf and was kept from going.

units.zh: 宿細人，不可使汙是官。
units.en: Su is a small man and must not defile it.
units.literal: Su is a petty man—he must not be allowed to stain that office.

units.zh: 後逢吉罷，詔權知諫議大夫，宰相崔群、王涯同請曰：「諫議大夫，前世或自山林、擢行伍任之者，然皆道義卓異於時。
units.en: After Fengji's fall an edict made Su acting Left Remonstrator; Cui Qun and Wang Ya petitioned together: "Remonstrators of old came from reclusion or the army, yet all stood out in conduct.
units.literal: Later when Fengji fell, an edict made Su acting Remonstrator of the Left; chancellors Cui Qun and Wang Ya jointly petitioned: "The remonstrator of old was sometimes taken from mountain forests or promoted from the ranks, yet all were outstanding in conduct for their age.

units.zh: 今宿望輕，若待以不次，未足以寵，適以累之也。」
units.en: Su's standing is light; an exceptional appointment will not honor him—only harm him."
units.literal: Now Su's reputation is slight; if you favor him with an extraordinary appointment, it is not enough to honor him—it only harms him."

units.zh: 玄誌卒，副將李正己殺其子，共推希逸，有詔就拜節度使，兼御史大夫。
units.en: When Xuanzhi died, deputy Li Zhengji killed his son and the army acclaimed Xiyi; he was appointed military governor on the spot and made grand censor as well.
units.literal: When Xuanzhi died, the deputy general Li Zhengji killed his son; together they pushed Xiyi forward, and an edict appointed him on the spot as Military Governor, concurrently Grand Censor.

units.zh: 夜與巫家野次，李正己因眾怨閉闔不內，遂奔滑州。
units.en: One night he camped in the open with a shaman's household; Li Zhengji, playing on popular anger, shut him out of the city, and he fled to Huazhou.
units.literal: One night he lodged in the open country with a shaman's family; Li Zhengji, relying on popular resentment, shut the gates and would not admit him, and he thereupon fled to Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 太和初，李同捷據滄德叛，智興上章，請躬督士卒討賊。
units.en: Early in the Taihe reign, Li Tongjie rebelled and held Cang and De; Zhixing memorialized the throne asking to lead the troops in person against the rebels.
units.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Li Tongjie held Cang and De in rebellion; Zhixing submitted a memorial requesting to personally oversee the soldiers in punishing the rebels.

units.zh: 初，同捷狂桀犯命，濟之以王廷湊，王師經年無功。
units.en: At first Tongjie's wild defiance of orders was sustained by aid from Wang Tingcou, and the imperial armies had failed for years.
units.literal: At first Tongjie was wild and defiant in offending orders; he was aided by Wang Tingcou; the imperial army for years had no success.

units.zh: 晏平幼從父征伐，以討李同捷功，授檢校右散騎常侍、靈州大都督府長史、朔方靈鹽節度。
units.en: Yanping campaigned with his father from youth and, for his service against Li Tongjie, was appointed acting right regular attendant, chief administrator of the Lingzhou protectorate, and military governor of Shuofang Ling and Salt.
units.literal: Yanping from youth followed his father on campaigns; for merit in punishing Li Tongjie he was appointed Acting Right Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Chief Administrator of the Great Protectorate Prefecture of Ling Prefecture, and military governor of Shuofang Ling and Salt.
